bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 起昭陽作噩，盡屠維單閼，凡七年。

translations.literal: From Zhaoyang Zuoe through Tuwei Shanque; seven years in all.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhaoyang Zuoe through Tuwei Shanque—seven years in all.

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，辛丑，葬孝宣皇帝於杜陵；

translations.literal: 1. In spring, the first month, on xinchou, Emperor Xiao Xuan was buried at Duling;
translations.idiomatic: 1. In spring, the first month, on xinchou, Emperor Xuan was buried at Duling;

sentences.zh: 赦天下。

translations.literal: a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: the empire was pardoned.

sentences.zh: ----2三月，丙午，立皇后王氏，封-{后父}-禁為陽平候。

translations.literal: ----2 In the third month, on bingwu, Empress Wang was installed; Wang -{后父}- Jin was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 In the third month, on bingwu, Empress Wang was installed; Wang -{后父}- Jin was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yangping.

sentences.zh: ----3以三輔、太常、郡國公田及苑可省者振業貧民；

translations.literal: ----3 Using public fields of the Three Metropolises, the Grand Music Master, commanderies and kingdoms, and parks that could be reduced, to revive the livelihood of poor commoners;
translations.idiomatic: ----3 Public fields of the Three Metropolises, the Grand Music Master, commanderies and kingdoms, and reducible imperial parks were used to revive the livelihood of the poor;

sentences.zh: 貲不滿千錢者，賦貸種、食。

translations.literal: those whose assets did not reach a thousand cash were granted loans of seed and food.
translations.idiomatic: those with assets under a thousand cash were lent seed and food.

sentences.zh: ----4封外祖父平恩戴侯同產弟子中常侍許嘉為平恩侯。

translations.literal: ----4 The younger brother by the same mother of the emperor's maternal grandfather, Marquis Dai of Ping'en, Palace Attendant Xu Jia, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Ping'en.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 Palace Attendant Xu Jia, younger brother by the same mother of the emperor's maternal grandfather, Marquis Dai of Ping'en, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Ping'en.

sentences.zh: ----5夏，六月，以民疾疫，令太官損膳，減樂府員，省苑馬，以振困乏。

translations.literal: ----5 In summer, the sixth month, because the people suffered pestilence, the Grand Provisioner was ordered to reduce meals, Music Bureau staff were cut, park horses were reduced, to relieve the distressed.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 In summer, the sixth month, because pestilence afflicted the people, the court ordered the Grand Provisioner to reduce meals, cut Music Bureau staff, and reduce park horses to relieve the distressed.

sentences.zh: ----6秋，九月，關東郡、國十一大水，饑，或人相食；

translations.literal: ----6 In autumn, the ninth month, eleven commanderies and kingdoms east of the Pass suffered great floods; there was famine, and in places men ate one another;
translations.idiomatic: ----6 In autumn, the ninth month, eleven commanderies and kingdoms east of the Pass were inundated; famine followed, and in places men ate one another;

sentences.zh: 轉旁郡錢穀以相救。

translations.literal: money and grain from neighboring commanderies were transferred to rescue one another.
translations.idiomatic: money and grain from neighboring commanderies were transferred for mutual relief.

sentences.zh: ----7上素聞琅邪王吉、貢禹皆明經潔行，遣使者徵之。

translations.literal: ----7 The emperor had long heard that Wang Ji of Langye and Gong Yu were both versed in the classics with pure conduct; he sent envoys to summon them.
translations.idiomatic: ----7 The emperor had long heard that Wang Ji of Langye and Gong Yu were both versed in the classics and of pure conduct; he sent envoys to summon them.

sentences.zh: 吉道病卒。

translations.literal: Ji died of illness on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Ji died of illness on the road.

sentences.zh: 禹至，拜為諫大夫。

translations.literal: Yu arrived and was appointed Remonstrating Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Yu arrived and was appointed Remonstrating Grandee.

sentences.zh: 上數虛已問以政事，禹奏言：「古者人君節儉，什一而稅，無它賦役，故家給人足。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly humbled himself to ask about government affairs. Yu memorialized: "In antiquity rulers were frugal, taxed one-tenth, and had no other levies or corvée; thus families were provided for and the people had enough.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repeatedly humbled himself to ask about government affairs. Yu memorialized: "In antiquity rulers were frugal, taxed one-tenth, and had no other levies or corvée—families were provided for and the people had enough.

sentences.zh: 高祖、孝文、孝景皇帝，宮女不過十餘人，廄馬百餘匹。

translations.literal: Emperors Gaozu, Xiaowen, and Xiaojing had palace women not exceeding a dozen-odd persons and stable horses a hundred-odd.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors Gaozu, Wen, and Jing kept no more than a dozen palace women and a hundred-odd stable horses.

sentences.zh: 後世爭為奢侈，轉轉益甚；

translations.literal: Later generations competed in luxury, turning ever more excessive;
translations.idiomatic: Later generations competed in luxury, each turn more excessive;

sentences.zh: 臣下亦相放效。

translations.literal: ministers below also imitated one another.
translations.idiomatic: officials below imitated one another as well.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為如太古難，宜少放古以自節焉。

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly thinks that matching high antiquity is difficult; it is fitting to release a little toward antiquity and restrain oneself.
translations.idiomatic: I foolishly think matching high antiquity is difficult; it would be fitting to ease somewhat toward antiquity and restrain oneself.

sentences.zh: 方今宮室已定，無可奈何矣；

translations.literal: Today palaces and halls are already fixed, and nothing can be done;
translations.idiomatic: Today the palaces are already fixed and nothing can be done about that;

sentences.zh: 其餘盡可減損。

translations.literal: the rest can all be reduced and cut.
translations.idiomatic: everything else can still be cut back.

sentences.zh: 故時齊三服官，輸物不過十笥；

translations.literal: In former times Qi's Three Garment Offices supplied goods not exceeding ten bamboo boxes;
translations.idiomatic: In former times Qi's Three Garment Offices sent no more than ten bamboo boxes of goods;

sentences.zh: 方今齊三服官，作工各數千人，一歲費數巨萬，廄馬食粟將萬匹。

translations.literal: today Qi's Three Garment Offices have several thousand workers at each workshop, costing tens of millions in one year; stable horses consume grain approaching ten thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: today Qi's Three Garment Offices employ thousands at each workshop, costing tens of millions a year; stable horses consume nearly ten thousand piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 武帝時，又多取好女至數千人，以填後宮。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Wu, he additionally took fine women numbering in the thousands to fill the rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu he took thousands of fine women to fill the rear palace.

sentences.zh: 及棄天下，多藏金錢、財物，鳥獸、魚鱉凡百九十物；

translations.literal: When he abandoned the realm, he hoarded much gold, cash, and valuables—birds, beasts, fish, and turtles, one hundred ninety kinds in all;
translations.idiomatic: When he left the realm he hoarded gold, cash, and valuables—birds, beasts, fish, and turtles, one hundred ninety kinds in all;

sentences.zh: 又皆以後宮女置於園陵。

translations.literal: moreover he stationed all rear-palace women at park-tombs.
translations.idiomatic: moreover he stationed rear-palace women at park-tombs.

sentences.zh: 至孝宣皇帝時，陛下惡有所言，群臣亦隨故事，甚可痛也！

translations.literal: At the time of Emperor Xiaoxuan, Your Majesty loathed speaking of such things, yet ministers also followed precedent—how deeply painful!
translations.idiomatic: At the time of Emperor Xuan, Your Majesty loathed speaking of such things, yet ministers still followed precedent—how painful!

sentences.zh: 故使天下承化，取女皆大過度，諸侯妻妾或至數百人，豪富吏民畜歌者至數十人，是以內多怨女，外多曠夫。

translations.literal: Thus the realm carried on the transformation: bride-taking everywhere far exceeded measure; feudal lords' wives and concubines sometimes reached hundreds; wealthy officials and commoners kept singers by the dozens—hence within were many resentful women and without many husbandless men.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the realm carried on the transformation: bride-taking everywhere far exceeded measure; feudal lords' wives and concubines sometimes reached hundreds; wealthy officials and commoners kept dozens of singers—within were many resentful women, without many husbandless men.

sentences.zh: 及眾庶葬埋，皆虛地上以實地下。

translations.literal: Among the masses as well, burials all emptied the above ground to fill the underground.
translations.idiomatic: Among the common people as well, burials emptied the living world to fill the grave.

sentences.zh: 其過自上生，皆在大臣循故事之罪也。

translations.literal: These excesses arose from above and were all the fault of great ministers who clung to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: These excesses arose from above and were chiefly the fault of great ministers who clung to precedent.

sentences.zh: 唯陛下深察古道，從其儉者。

translations.literal: Only Your Majesty would deeply examine the ancient Way and follow what is frugal.
translations.idiomatic: Only Your Majesty would deeply examine the ancient Way and follow what is frugal.

sentences.zh: 大減損乘輿服御器物，三分去二；

translations.literal: Greatly reduce and cut imperial carriages, robes, and implements—remove two parts in three;
translations.idiomatic: Greatly cut imperial carriages, robes, and implements—remove two parts in three;

sentences.zh: 擇後宮賢者，留二十人，餘悉歸之，及諸陵園女無子者，宜悉遣；

translations.literal: select the worthy among rear-palace women, retain twenty, return all the rest, and all tomb-park women without sons should be sent out;
translations.idiomatic: select the worthy among rear-palace women, retain twenty, return the rest, and send out all tomb-park women without sons;

sentences.zh: 廄馬可無過數十匹，獨捨長安城南苑地，以為田獵之囿。

translations.literal: stable horses need not exceed several dozen; only keep the park south of Chang'an for field and hunt.
translations.idiomatic: stable horses need not exceed several dozen; only keep the park south of Chang'an for hunting.

sentences.zh: 方今天下饑饉，可無大自損減以救之稱天意乎！

translations.literal: Today the realm suffers famine—can we not greatly reduce ourselves to deliver relief and match Heaven's intent!
translations.idiomatic: Today the realm suffers famine—can we not greatly reduce ourselves to deliver relief and match Heaven's intent!

sentences.zh: 天生聖人，蓋為萬民，非獨使自娛樂而已也。

translations.literal: Heaven born the sage to be for the myriad people—not merely for his own pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven born the sage for the myriad people—not merely for his own pleasure.

sentences.zh: 」天子納善其言，下詔，令諸宮館希御幸者勿繕治；

translations.literal: " The Son of Heaven accepted his good words and issued an edict: palace residences rarely favored by the emperor should not be repaired;
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor accepted his counsel and issued an edict: palace residences rarely visited by the emperor should not be repaired;

sentences.zh: 太僕減穀食馬；

translations.literal: the Grand Coachman reduced grain for horses;
translations.idiomatic: the Grand Coachman reduced grain for horses;

sentences.zh: 水衡省肉食獸。

translations.literal: the Office of Water and Parks cut meat-eating beasts.
translations.idiomatic: the Office of Water and Parks cut meat-eating beasts.

sentences.zh: :臣光曰：忠臣之事君也，責其所難，則其易者不勞而正；

translations.literal: : Your servant Guang says: When loyal ministers serve their ruler, they press what is difficult; then what is easy is corrected without labor;
translations.idiomatic: : Your servant Guang says: When loyal ministers serve their ruler, they press what is difficult; then what is easy is corrected without labor;

sentences.zh: 補其所短，則其長者不勸而遂。

translations.literal: they mend what is short; then what is long advances without exhortation.
translations.idiomatic: they mend what is short; then what is long advances without exhortation.

sentences.zh: 孝元踐位之初，虛心以問禹，禹宜先其所急，後其所緩。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaoyuan's accession, he humbly asked Yu; Yu should have put first what was urgent and afterward what could wait.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Yuan's accession, he humbly asked Yu; Yu should have put first what was urgent and afterward what could wait.

sentences.zh: 然則優遊不斷，讒佞用權，當時之大患也，而禹不以為言；

translations.literal: Yet lenient delay without decision, slanderers and flatterers wielding power—the great affliction of the time—and Yu did not speak of it;
translations.idiomatic: Yet lenient delay without decision and slanderers and flatterers wielding power were the great afflictions of the time, yet Yu did not speak of them;

sentences.zh: 恭謹節儉，孝元之素志也，而禹孜孜而言之，何哉！

translations.literal: respectful caution and frugality were Emperor Xiaoyuan's constant aim, yet Yu spoke of them tirelessly—why!
translations.idiomatic: respectful caution and frugality were Emperor Yuan's constant aim, yet Yu spoke of them tirelessly—why!

sentences.zh: 使禹之智足不以知，烏得為賢！

translations.literal: If Yu's wisdom sufficed yet he did not know, how could he be called worthy!
translations.idiomatic: If Yu's wisdom sufficed yet he did not know, how could he be called worthy!

sentences.zh: 知而不言，為罪愈大矣！

translations.literal: To know and not speak—the offense is all the greater!
translations.idiomatic: To know and not speak—the offense is all the greater!

sentences.zh: ----8匈奴呼韓邪單于復上書，言民眾困乏。

translations.literal: ----8 The Xiongnu chanyu Huhanye again submitted a memorial saying his people were distressed and depleted.
translations.idiomatic: ----8 The Xiongnu chanyu Huhanye again submitted a memorial saying his people were distressed and depleted.

sentences.zh: 詔雲中、五原郡轉穀二萬斛以給之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yunzhong and Wuyuan commanderies to transfer twenty thousand hu of grain to supply him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Yunzhong and Wuyuan commanderies to transfer twenty thousand hu of grain to supply him.

sentences.zh: ----9是歲，初置戊己校尉，使屯田車師故地。

translations.literal: ----9 That year, the Wuji Colonel was first established to garrison and farm the former territory of Cheshi.
translations.idiomatic: ----9 That year the Wuji Colonel was first established to garrison and farm the former territory of Cheshi.

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，上行幸甘泉，郊泰畤。

translations.literal: 1. In spring, the first month, the emperor traveled in favor to Sweet Springs and sacrificed at the border to the Great Altar.
translations.idiomatic: 1. In spring, the first month, the emperor traveled to Sweet Springs and sacrificed at the Great Altar.

sentences.zh: 樂陵侯史高以外屬領尚書事，前將軍蕭望之、光祿大夫周堪為之副。

translations.literal: Yue Ling Marquis Shi Gao, as maternal kin, headed Secretariat affairs; former General Xiao Wangzhi and Household Gentleman Zhou Kan served as his deputies.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Ling Marquis Shi Gao, as maternal kin, headed Secretariat affairs; former General Xiao Wangzhi and Household Gentleman Zhou Kan served as his deputies.

sentences.zh: 望之名儒，與堪皆以師傅舊恩，天子任之，數宴見，言治亂，陳王事。

translations.literal: Wangzhi was a renowned classicist; both he and Kan, through old favor as tutors, were trusted by the Son of Heaven, often received at banquets, spoke of order and disorder, and laid out royal affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wangzhi was a renowned classicist; both he and Kan, through old ties as tutors, were trusted by the emperor, often dined with him, discussed order and disorder, and laid out royal affairs.

sentences.zh: 望之選白宗室明經有行散騎、諫大夫劉更生給事中，與侍中金敞並拾遺左右。

translations.literal: Wangzhi nominated and reported Liu Gengsheng of the imperial clan, versed in the classics with conduct, as Cavalier Attendant and Remonstrating Grandee in the Palace Secretariat, together with Palace Attendant Jin Chang picking up what was neglected at the ruler's side.
translations.idiomatic: Wangzhi nominated Liu Gengsheng of the imperial clan, versed in the classics and of good conduct, as Cavalier Attendant and Remonstrating Grandee in the Palace Secretariat; he and Palace Attendant Jin Chang picked up what was neglected at the emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 四人同心謀議，勸導上以古制，多所欲匡正；

translations.literal: The four men united in counsel, urging the ruler toward ancient institutions and wanting much to correct abuses;
translations.idiomatic: The four men united in counsel, urging the emperor toward ancient institutions and wanting much to correct abuses;

sentences.zh: 上甚鄉納之。

translations.literal: the emperor greatly inclined to accept them.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor greatly inclined to accept them.

sentences.zh: 史高充位而已，由此與望之有隙。

translations.literal: Shi Gao merely filled a post; from this he bore a rift with Wangzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Gao merely filled a post; from this he bore a rift with Wangzhi.

sentences.zh: 中書令弘恭、僕射石顯，自宣帝時久典樞機，明習文法；

translations.literal: Palace Secretariat Director Hong Gong and Vice Director Shi Xian, from Emperor Xuan's time, had long held the pivot of power and were skilled in written law;
translations.idiomatic: Palace Secretariat Director Hong Gong and Vice Director Shi Xian had long held the pivot of power from Emperor Xuan's time and were skilled in written law;

sentences.zh: 帝即位多疾，以顯久典事，中人無外黨，精專可信任，遂委以政，事無小大，因顯白決，貴幸傾朝，百僚皆敬事顯。

translations.literal: when the emperor took the throne he was often ill; because Xian had long managed affairs and the inner attendants had no external faction and were dedicated and trustworthy, government was entrusted to him—matters great or small were decided as Xian reported upward; honored and favored, he dominated the court, and all officials honored and served Xian.
translations.idiomatic: when the emperor took the throne he was often ill; because Xian had long managed affairs and the inner attendants had no external faction and were dedicated and trustworthy, he entrusted him with government—matters great or small were decided as Xian reported upward; honored and favored, he dominated the court, and all officials honored and served Xian.

sentences.zh: 顯為人巧慧習事，能深得人主微指，內深賊，持詭辯，以中傷人，忤恨睚眥，輒被以危法；

translations.literal: Xian as a man was clever and practiced in affairs, able to grasp the ruler's subtle intent; inwardly deeply malicious, he wielded deceptive argument to strike at men; for the smallest grudge he would cloak them in deadly law;
translations.idiomatic: Xian was clever and practiced in affairs, able to grasp the ruler's subtle intent; inwardly deeply malicious, he wielded deceptive argument to strike at men; for the smallest grudge he would cloak opponents in deadly law;

sentences.zh: 亦與車騎將軍高為表裡，議論常獨持故事，不從望之等。

translations.literal: he also worked hand in glove with General of Chariots and Cavalry Gao; in discussion they usually held alone to precedent and did not follow Wangzhi and the others.
translations.idiomatic: he also worked hand in glove with General of Chariots and Cavalry Gao; in discussion they usually held alone to precedent and did not follow Wangzhi and the others.

sentences.zh: 望之等患苦許、史放縱，又疾恭、顯擅權，建白以為：「中書政本，國家樞機，宜以通明公正處之。

translations.literal: Wangzhi and his circle were distressed at Xu and Shi clans' license and hated that Gong and Xian monopolized power; they memorialized: "The Secretariat is the root of government and the state's pivot; it should be run with luminous fairness.
translations.idiomatic: Wangzhi and his circle were distressed at the Xu and Shi clans' license and hated that Gong and Xian monopolized power; they memorialized: "The Secretariat is the root of government and the state's pivot; it should be run with luminous fairness.

sentences.zh: 武帝游宴後庭，故用宦者，非古制也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu held banquets in the rear court he employed eunuchs—this is not the ancient system.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu held banquets in the rear court he employed eunuchs—this is not the ancient system.

sentences.zh: 宜罷中書宦官，應古不近刑人之義。

translations.literal: Eunuchs in the Secretariat should be abolished, in keeping with antiquity's rule that those near punishment should not hold power.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs in the Secretariat should be abolished, in keeping with antiquity's rule that those near punishment should not hold power.

sentences.zh: 」由是大與高、恭、顯忤。

translations.literal: " From this they sharply clashed with Gao, Gong, and Xian.
translations.idiomatic: " From this they sharply clashed with Gao, Gong, and Xian.

sentences.zh: 上初即位，謙讓，重改作，議久不定，出劉更生為宗正。

translations.literal: The emperor, newly enthroned, was modest and reluctant and regarded reorganization as weighty; the debate long went unsettled, and Liu Gengsheng was sent out as Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, newly enthroned, was modest and reluctant and regarded reorganization as weighty; the debate long went unsettled, and Liu Gengsheng was sent out as Director of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 望之、堪數薦名儒、茂材以備諫官，會稽鄭朋陰欲附望之，上書言車騎將軍高遣客為奸利郡國，及言許、史弟子罪過。

translations.literal: Wangzhi and Kan repeatedly recommended renowned classicists and exceptional talent for remonstrance offices. Kuaiji's Zheng Peng secretly wished to attach himself to Wangzhi and memorialized that General of Chariots and Cavalry Gao's clients did illicit profit in commanderies and kingdoms, and cited crimes of Xu and Shi clan youths.
translations.idiomatic: Wangzhi and Kan repeatedly recommended renowned classicists and exceptional talent for remonstrance offices. Kuaiji's Zheng Peng secretly wished to attach himself to Wangzhi and memorialized that General of Chariots and Cavalry Gao's clients did illicit profit in commanderies and kingdoms, and cited crimes of Xu and Shi clan youths.

sentences.zh: 章視周堪，堪白：「令朋待詔金馬門。

translations.literal: The memorial was shown to Zhou Kan; Kan reported: "Let Peng await summons at the Golden Horse Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was shown to Zhou Kan; Kan reported: "Let Peng await summons at the Golden Horse Gate.

sentences.zh: 」朋奏記望之曰：「今將軍規模，-{云}-若管、晏而休，遂行日昃，至周、召乃留乎？

translations.literal: " Peng submitted a memorial-note to Wangzhi, saying: "Now the general's scope—-{云}- if like Guan Zhong and Yan Ying you then stop, will you halt at sunset only when you reach the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao?
translations.idiomatic: " Peng submitted a memorial-note to Wangzhi, saying: "Now the general's scope—-{云}- if like Guan Zhong and Yan Ying you then stop, will you halt at sunset only when you reach the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao?

sentences.zh: 若管、晏而休，則下走將歸延陵之皋，沒齒而已矣。

translations.literal: If you stop at Guan and Yan, your subordinates below will go home to Yanling's shore and till to the end of their days.
translations.idiomatic: If you stop at Guan and Yan, your subordinates below will go home to Yanling's shore and till to the end of their days.

sentences.zh: 如將軍興周、召之遺業，親日昃之兼聽，則下走其庶幾願竭區區奉萬分之一！

translations.literal: But if the general takes up the legacy of the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao, personally attending from morning to night with broad hearing, then your subordinates below would scarcely dare hope to exhaust their petty strength for even one part in ten thousand!
translations.idiomatic: But if the general takes up the legacy of the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao, personally attending from morning to night with broad hearing, then your subordinates below would scarcely dare hope to exhaust their petty strength for even one part in ten thousand!

sentences.zh: 」望之始見朋，接待以意；

translations.literal: " Wangzhi at first received Peng with attention;
translations.idiomatic: " Wangzhi at first received Peng with attention;

sentences.zh: 後知其傾邪，絕不與通。

translations.literal: later learning he was crooked, he cut him off entirely.
translations.idiomatic: later learning he was crooked, he cut him off entirely.

sentences.zh: 朋，楚士，怨恨，更求入許、史，推所言許、史事，曰：「皆周堪、劉更生教我；

translations.literal: Peng, a man of Chu, bore resentment, sought entry among Xu and Shi, and pushed claims about Xu and Shi affairs, saying: "All of it Zhou Kan and Liu Gengsheng taught me;
translations.idiomatic: Peng, a man of Chu, bore resentment, sought entry among Xu and Shi, and pushed claims about Xu and Shi affairs, saying: "All of it Zhou Kan and Liu Gengsheng taught me;

sentences.zh: 我關東人，何以知此！

translations.literal: I am a man east of the Pass—how would I know this!
translations.idiomatic: I am a man east of the Pass—how would I know this!

sentences.zh: 」於是侍中許章白見朋。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Palace Attendant Xu Zhang had Peng brought to audience.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon Palace Attendant Xu Zhang had Peng brought to audience.

sentences.zh: 朋出，揚言曰：「我見言前將軍小過五，大罪一。

translations.literal: Peng came out and proclaimed: "I told of five small faults and one great crime of the former general.
translations.idiomatic: Peng came out and proclaimed: "I told of five small faults and one great crime of the former general.

sentences.zh: 」待詔華龍行污穢，欲入堪等，堪等不納，亦與朋相結。

translations.literal: " Attendant Hua Long practiced filth and wanted to join Kan's faction; they would not take him in, yet he allied with Peng as well.
translations.idiomatic: " Attendant Hua Long practiced filth and wanted to join Kan's faction; they would not take him in, yet he allied with Peng as well.

sentences.zh: 恭、顯令二人告望之等謀欲罷車騎將軍，疏退許、史狀，候望之出休日，令朋、龍上之。

translations.literal: Gong and Xian had the two men accuse Wangzhi and company of plotting to remove General of Chariots and Cavalry Gao and of memorializing to push aside Xu and Shi; they waited for Wangzhi's day off and had Peng and Long submit it.
translations.idiomatic: Gong and Xian had the two men accuse Wangzhi and company of plotting to remove General of Chariots and Cavalry Gao and of memorializing to push aside Xu and Shi; they waited for Wangzhi's day off and had Peng and Long submit it.

sentences.zh: 事下弘恭問狀，望之對曰：「外戚在位多奢淫，欲以匡正國家，非為邪也。

translations.literal: The matter went down to Hong Gong for inquiry. Wangzhi answered: "The outer kin in office are mostly extravagant—the aim is to correct the state, not to do evil.
translations.idiomatic: The matter went down to Hong Gong for inquiry. Wangzhi answered: "The outer kin in office are mostly extravagant—the aim is to correct the state, not to do evil.

sentences.zh: 」恭、顯奏：「望之、堪、更生朋黨相稱舉，數譖訴大臣，毀離親戚，欲以專擅權勢。

translations.literal: " Gong and Xian memorialized: "Wangzhi, Kan, and Gengsheng formed a faction praising one another, repeatedly slandering great ministers, tearing apart relatives, wishing to monopolize power.
translations.idiomatic: " Gong and Xian memorialized: "Wangzhi, Kan, and Gengsheng formed a faction praising one another, repeatedly slandering great ministers, tearing apart relatives, wishing to monopolize power.

sentences.zh: 為臣不忠，誣上不道，請謁者召致廷尉。

translations.literal: As ministers unloyal, deceiving the throne and impious, they ask that the courier summon them to the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: As ministers unloyal, deceiving the throne and impious, they ask that the courier summon them to the Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 」時上初即位，不省召致廷尉為下獄也，可其奏。

translations.literal: " At the time the emperor, newly enthroned, did not understand that "summon to the Minister of Justice" meant imprisonment and approved the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time the emperor, newly enthroned, did not understand that "summon to the Minister of Justice" meant imprisonment and approved the memorial.

sentences.zh: 後上召堪、更生，曰：「繫獄。

translations.literal: Later the emperor summoned Kan and Gengsheng and said: "Imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor summoned Kan and Gengsheng and said: "Imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 」上大驚曰：「非但廷尉問邪！

translations.literal: " The emperor was greatly alarmed: "Not merely inquiry by the Minister of Justice!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was greatly alarmed: "Not merely inquiry by the Minister of Justice!

sentences.zh: 」以責恭、顯，皆叩頭謝。

translations.literal: " He reproached Gong and Xian, who all knocked their heads in apology.
translations.idiomatic: " He reproached Gong and Xian, who all knocked their heads in apology.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「令出視事。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Let them go out and resume duties.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Let them go out and resume duties.

sentences.zh: 」恭、顯因使史高言：「上新即位，未以德化聞於天下，而先驗師傅。

translations.literal: " Gong and Xian then had Shi Gao speak: "Your Majesty is newly enthroned and has not yet made your virtue heard throughout the realm, yet you first try your tutors.
translations.idiomatic: " Gong and Xian then had Shi Gao speak: "Your Majesty is newly enthroned and has not yet made your virtue heard throughout the realm, yet you first try your tutors.

sentences.zh: 既下九卿、大夫獄，宜因決免。

translations.literal: They are already down in the Nine Ministers and Grandees' prison—it is fitting to decide and dismiss them.
translations.idiomatic: They are already down in the Nine Ministers and Grandees' prison—it is fitting to decide and dismiss them.

sentences.zh: 」於是制詔丞相、御史：「前將軍望之，傅朕八年，無它罪過。

translations.literal: " Thereupon an edict to Chancellor and Censor: "Former general Wangzhi tutored Us eight years without other fault.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon an edict to Chancellor and Censor: "Former general Wangzhi tutored Us eight years without other fault.

sentences.zh: 今事久遠，識忘難明，其赦望之罪，收前將軍、光祿勳印綬；

translations.literal: The matter is long past and memory hard to clear—pardon Wangzhi's crime and take back the seals of Former General and Household Gentleman;
translations.idiomatic: The matter is long past and memory hard to clear—pardon Wangzhi's crime and take back the seals of Former General and Household Gentleman;

sentences.zh: 及堪、更生皆免為庶人。

translations.literal: Kan and Gengsheng are all demoted to commoners."
translations.idiomatic: Kan and Gengsheng are all demoted to commoners."

sentences.zh: 」----2二月，丁巳，立弟竟為清河王。

translations.literal: " ----2 In the second month, on dingsi, the emperor's younger brother Jing was installed as King of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: " ----2 In the second month, on dingsi, the emperor's younger brother Jing was installed as King of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: ----3戊午，隴西地震，敗城郭、屋室，壓殺人眾。

translations.literal: ----3 On wuwu, Longxi suffered an earthquake that destroyed walls and houses and crushed many to death.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 On wuwu, Longxi suffered an earthquake that destroyed walls and houses and crushed many to death.

sentences.zh: ----4三月，立廣陵厲王子霸為王。

translations.literal: ----4 In the third month, the son of the deposed King of Guangling, Ba, was installed as king.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 In the third month, the son of the deposed King of Guangling, Ba, was installed as king.

sentences.zh: ----5詔罷黃門乘輿狗馬，水衡禁囿、宜春下苑、少府佽飛外池、嚴籞池田假與貧民。

translations.literal: ----5 An edict abolished Yellow Gate carriage dogs and horses; the Offices of Water and Parks, Yichun Lower Park, Lesser Treasury flying outer pools, and strict park pool fields were rented to poor commoners.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 An edict abolished Yellow Gate carriage dogs and horses; the Offices of Water and Parks, Yichun Lower Park, Lesser Treasury flying outer pools, and strict park pool fields were rented to poor commoners.

sentences.zh: 又詔赦天下，舉茂材異等、直言極諫之士。

translations.literal: Another edict pardoned the realm and raised exceptional talent of unusual grade and men of blunt remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict pardoned the realm and raised exceptional talent of unusual grade and men of blunt remonstrance.

sentences.zh: ----6夏，四月，丁巳，立子驁為皇太子。

translations.literal: ----6 In summer, the fourth month, on dingsi, son Ao was installed as Imperial Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: ----6 In summer, the fourth month, on dingsi, son Ao was installed as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 待詔鄭朋薦太原太守張敞，先帝名臣，宜傅輔皇太子。

translations.literal: Attendant Zheng Peng recommended Taiyuan governor Zhang Chang, an esteemed minister of the former emperor, as fit to tutor and assist the Imperial Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Zheng Peng recommended Taiyuan governor Zhang Chang, an esteemed minister of the former emperor, as fit to tutor and assist the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 上以問蕭望之，望之以為敞能吏，任治煩亂，材輕，非師傅之器。

translations.literal: The emperor asked Xiao Wangzhi; Wangzhi thought Chang a capable official for troubled governance but light in talent—not material for a tutor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Xiao Wangzhi; Wangzhi thought Chang a capable official for troubled governance but light in talent—not material for a tutor.

sentences.zh: 天子使使者徵敞，欲以為左馮翊，會病卒。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven sent a courier to summon Chang, wishing to make him Left Governor of Feng, but he died of illness en route.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a courier to summon Chang, wishing to make him Left Governor of Feng, but he died of illness en route.

sentences.zh: ----7詔賜蕭望之爵關內侯，給事中，朝朔望。

translations.literal: ----7 An edict granted Xiao Wangzhi the rank of Marquis within the Passes, appointment in the Palace Secretariat, and attendance on the first and fifteenth of the month.
translations.idiomatic: ----7 An edict granted Xiao Wangzhi the rank of Marquis within the Passes, appointment in the Palace Secretariat, and attendance on the first and fifteenth of the month.

sentences.zh: ----8關東饑，齊地人相食。

translations.literal: ----8 East of the Pass suffered famine; in Qi territory people ate one another.
translations.idiomatic: ----8 East of the Pass suffered famine; in Qi territory people ate one another.

sentences.zh: ----9秋，七月，己酉，地復震。

translations.literal: ----9 Autumn, seventh month, day jiyou: the earth quaked again.
translations.idiomatic: ----9 In autumn, the seventh month, on day jiyou, the earth quaked again.

sentences.zh: ----10上復征周堪、劉更生，欲以為諫大夫；

translations.literal: ----10 The emperor again summoned Zhou Kan and Liu Gengsheng, wishing to make them Remonstrance Grandees;
translations.idiomatic: ----10 The emperor again summoned Zhou Kan and Liu Gengsheng, wishing to make them Remonstrance Grandees;

sentences.zh: 弘恭、石顯白，皆以為中郎。

translations.literal: Hong Gong and Shi Xian reported, and all were made Gentlemen of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Gong and Shi Xian reported against it, and all were made Gentlemen of the Palace instead.

sentences.zh: 上器重蕭望之不已，欲倚以為相；

translations.literal: The emperor valued Xiao Wangzhi without cease and wished to rely on him as chancellor;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor valued Xiao Wangzhi without cease and wished to rely on him as chancellor;

sentences.zh: 恭、顯及許、史子弟、侍中、諸曹皆側目於望之等。

translations.literal: Gong, Xian, and the Xu and Shi clans' sons and younger brothers, palace attendants, and the various bureaus all glared sidelong at Wangzhi and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Gong, Xian, and the Xu and Shi clans' sons and younger brothers, palace attendants, and the various bureaus all glared sidelong at Wangzhi and his circle.

sentences.zh: 更生乃使其外親上變事，言「地震殆為恭等，不為三獨夫動。

translations.literal: Gengsheng then had a maternal relative submit a report of irregularity, saying "The earthquake was probably for Gong and the rest, not moved by the three lone men.
translations.idiomatic: Gengsheng then had a maternal relative submit a report of irregularity, saying, "The earthquake was probably on account of Gong and the rest, not stirred by the three lone men.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為宜退恭、顯以章蔽善之罰，進望之等以通賢者之路。

translations.literal: Your servant is foolish and thinks one ought to dismiss Gong and Xian to make clear the punishment for screening out the good, and advance Wangzhi and the rest to open the road for the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant thinks one ought to dismiss Gong and Xian to make clear the punishment for screening out the good, and advance Wangzhi and the rest to open the road for the worthy.

sentences.zh: 如此，則太平之門開，災異之原塞矣。

translations.literal: If so, then the gate of great peace would open and the source of portents and anomalies would be blocked.
translations.idiomatic: If so, the gate of great peace would open and the source of portents and anomalies would be blocked.

sentences.zh: 」書奏，恭、顯疑其更生所為，白請考奸詐，辭果服；

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, Gong and Xian suspected Gengsheng had done it and reported requesting investigation for treachery and fraud; under interrogation the words indeed matched;
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial was submitted, Gong and Xian suspected Gengsheng had done it and requested investigation for treachery and fraud; under interrogation the confession indeed matched;

sentences.zh: 遂逮更生繫獄，免為庶人。

translations.literal: Gengsheng was thereupon arrested and imprisoned, and dismissed as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Gengsheng was thereupon arrested and imprisoned, and dismissed as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 會望之子散騎、中郎人及亦上書訟望之前事，事下有司，復奏：「望之前所坐明白，無譖訴者，而教子上書，稱引亡辜之詩，失大臣體，不敬，請逮捕。

translations.literal: It happened that Wangzhi's son Sanqi and Gentleman of the Palace Ren Ji also submitted a memorial suing over Wangzhi's former case; the matter was sent down to the officials, who again memorialized: "Wangzhi's former offense was clear and there was no false accusation, yet he taught his son to submit a memorial, citing poems of the guiltless dead—losing a great minister's bearing, disrespectful; we request arrest.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Wangzhi's son Sanqi and Gentleman of the Palace Ren Ji also memorialized suing over Wangzhi's former case; the matter was sent to the officials, who again reported, "Wangzhi's former offense was clear and there was no false accusation, yet he taught his son to submit a memorial citing poems of the guiltless dead—losing a great minister's bearing and showing disrespect; we request arrest.

sentences.zh: 」弘恭、石顯等知望之素高節，不詘辱，建白：「望之前幸得不坐，復賜爵邑，不悔過服罪，深懷怨望，教子上書，歸非於上，自以托師傅，終必不坐，非頗屈望之於牢獄，塞其怏怏心，則聖朝無以施恩厚。

translations.literal: " Hong Gong, Shi Xian, and the rest knew Wangzhi by nature had lofty integrity and would not submit to humiliation, and proposed: "Wangzhi before fortunately escaped punishment, again received noble rank and fief, did not repent and accept guilt, deeply harbored resentment, taught his son to submit a memorial, and attributed blame to the emperor—trusting that as one who relied on the imperial tutor he would in the end certainly not be punished. Unless Wangzhi is somewhat bent in prison to stop up his resentful heart, the sagely court has no way to bestow generous grace.
translations.idiomatic: " Hong Gong, Shi Xian, and the rest knew Wangzhi by nature had lofty integrity and would not submit to humiliation, and proposed, "Wangzhi before fortunately escaped punishment and again received noble rank and fief, yet did not repent and accept guilt, deeply harbored resentment, taught his son to memorialize, and attributed blame to the emperor—trusting that as imperial tutor he would in the end certainly not be punished. Unless Wangzhi is somewhat bent in prison to stop up his resentful heart, the sagely court has no way to bestow generous grace.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「蕭太傅素剛，安肯就吏！

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Grand Tutor Xiao is by nature firm—how would he consent to go to the officials!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Grand Tutor Xiao is by nature firm—how would he consent to go to the officials!

sentences.zh: 」顯等曰：「人命至重，望之所坐，語言薄罪，必無所憂。

translations.literal: " Xian and the rest said: "Human life is utmostly weighty; what Wangzhi sits in is a slight offense of words—he will certainly have no worry.
translations.idiomatic: " Xian and the rest said, "Human life is utmostly weighty; what Wangzhi sits in is a slight offense of words—he will certainly have no worry.

sentences.zh: 」上乃可其奏。

translations.literal: " The emperor thereupon approved their memorial.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor thereupon approved their memorial.

sentences.zh: 冬，十二月，顯等封詔以付謁者，敕令召望之手付。

translations.literal: Winter, twelfth month: Xian and the rest sealed the edict and gave it to the usher, ordering him to summon Wangzhi and hand it to him in person.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the twelfth month, Xian and the rest sealed the edict and gave it to the usher, ordering him to summon Wangzhi and hand it to him in person.

sentences.zh: 因令太常急發執金吾車騎馳圍其第。

translations.literal: They then ordered the Grand Minister of Ceremonies urgently to dispatch the Commandant of the Metropolitan Area's chariots and horsemen to gallop and surround his residence.
translations.idiomatic: They then ordered the Grand Minister of Ceremonies urgently to dispatch the Commandant of the Metropolitan Area's chariots and horsemen to gallop and surround his residence.

sentences.zh: 使者至，召望之。

translations.literal: When the envoy arrived, he summoned Wangzhi.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy arrived, he summoned Wangzhi.

sentences.zh: 望之以問門下生魯國朱雲，雲者，好節士，勸望之自裁。

translations.literal: Wangzhi questioned his gate student Zhu Yun of Lu about it; Yun was one who loved men of integrity and urged Wangzhi to take his own life.
translations.idiomatic: Wangzhi asked his gate student Zhu Yun of Lu about it; Yun, who loved men of integrity, urged Wangzhi to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 於是望之仰天歎曰：「吾嘗備位將相，年逾六十矣，老入牢獄，苟求生活，不亦鄙乎！

translations.literal: Thereupon Wangzhi looked up to heaven and sighed, saying: "I once filled the rank of general and minister; I am past sixty. To grow old entering prison and basely seeking to live—would that not be base!
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Wangzhi looked up to heaven and sighed, "I once filled the rank of general and minister; I am past sixty. To grow old entering prison and basely seeking to live—would that not be base!

sentences.zh: 」字謂雲曰：「游，趣和藥來，無久留我死！

translations.literal: " He addressed Yun by his style name, saying: "You—hurry and bring the poisoned draught; do not long detain my death!
translations.idiomatic: " He addressed Yun by his style name, saying, "You—hurry and bring the poisoned draught; do not long detain my death!

sentences.zh: 」竟飲鳩自殺。

translations.literal: " In the end he drank bane and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end he drank bane and killed himself.

sentences.zh: 天子聞之驚，拊手曰：「曩固疑其不就牢獄，果然殺吾賢傅！

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven, hearing it, was startled and clapped his hands, saying: "Before I indeed doubted he would not go to prison—he has truly killed my worthy tutor!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, hearing it, was startled and clapped his hands, saying, "Before I indeed doubted he would not go to prison—he has truly killed my worthy tutor!

sentences.zh: 」是時，太官方上晝食，上乃卻食，為之涕泣，哀動左右。

translations.literal: " At that time the Grand Steward was just serving the midday meal; the emperor thereupon pushed the meal away, wept tears for him, and his grief moved those at his side.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time the Grand Steward was just serving the midday meal; the emperor pushed the meal away, wept for him, and his grief moved those at his side.

sentences.zh: 於是召顯等責問；

translations.literal: Thereupon he summoned Xian and the rest to rebuke and question them;
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he summoned Xian and the rest to rebuke and question them;

sentences.zh: 以議不詳，皆免冠謝，良久然後已。

translations.literal: because their deliberation had not been thorough, all removed their caps and apologized; only after a long while did he stop.
translations.idiomatic: because their deliberation had not been thorough, all removed their caps and apologized; only after a long while did he stop.

sentences.zh: 上追念望之不忘，每歲時遣使者祠祭望之塚，終帝之世。

translations.literal: The emperor, recalling Wangzhi without forgetting, every year at the seasons sent envoys to sacrifice at Wangzhi's tomb—throughout the emperor's reign.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, recalling Wangzhi without forgetting, every year at the seasons sent envoys to sacrifice at Wangzhi's tomb throughout his reign.

sentences.zh: :臣光曰：甚矣孝元之為君，易欺而難寤也！

translations.literal: : Your servant Guang says: How extreme was Emperor Xiao Yuan as ruler—easy to deceive and hard to awaken!
translations.idiomatic: : Your servant Guang says: How extreme was Emperor Yuan as ruler—easy to deceive and hard to awaken!

sentences.zh: 夫恭、顯之譖訴望之，其邪說詭計，誠有所不能辨也。

translations.literal: As for Gong and Xian's false accusations against Wangzhi, their perverse words and deceitful schemes—there truly were things he could not distinguish.
translations.idiomatic: As for Gong and Xian's false accusations against Wangzhi, their perverse words and deceitful schemes—there truly were things he could not distinguish.

sentences.zh: 至於始疑望之不肯就獄，恭、顯以為必無憂。

translations.literal: As for his first doubting that Wangzhi would not consent to go to prison, and Gong and Xian thinking he would certainly have no worry—
translations.idiomatic: As for his first doubting that Wangzhi would not consent to go to prison, and Gong and Xian thinking he would certainly have no worry—

sentences.zh: 已而果自殺，則恭、顯之欺亦明矣。

translations.literal: yet afterward he indeed killed himself—then Gong and Xian's deception was also clear.
translations.idiomatic: yet afterward he indeed killed himself—then Gong and Xian's deception was also clear.

sentences.zh: 在中智之君，孰不感動奮發以厎邪臣之罰！

translations.literal: In a ruler of middling wisdom, who would not be moved and roused to apply the punishment to wicked ministers!
translations.idiomatic: In a ruler of middling wisdom, who would not be moved and roused to punish wicked ministers!

sentences.zh: 孝元則不然。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiao Yuan was not so.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan was not so.

sentences.zh: 雖涕泣不食以傷望之，而終不能誅恭、顯，才得其免冠謝而已。

translations.literal: Though he wept, refused food, and grieved for Wangzhi, in the end he could not execute Gong and Xian—he only got their removing caps and apologizing, and that was all.
translations.idiomatic: Though he wept, refused food, and grieved for Wangzhi, in the end he could not execute Gong and Xian—he only got them to remove their caps and apologize, and that was all.

sentences.zh: 如此，則奸臣安所懲乎！

translations.literal: If so, where would wicked ministers be punished!
translations.idiomatic: If so, where would wicked ministers be punished!

sentences.zh: 是使恭、顯得肆其邪心而無復忌憚者也。

translations.literal: This was what let Gong and Xian unleash their wicked hearts without further fear or restraint.
translations.idiomatic: This was what let Gong and Xian unleash their wicked hearts without further fear or restraint.

sentences.zh: ----11是歲，弘恭病死，石顯為中書令。

translations.literal: ----11 That year Hong Gong died of illness; Shi Xian became Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: ----11 That year Hong Gong died of illness; Shi Xian became Director of the Palace Secretariat.

translations.literal: ----12 Initially, when Emperor Wu destroyed Nanyue, he opened and established Zhuya and Dan'er commanderies on islands in the sea; clerks and soldiers were all men of the central states and often encroached on and bullied the people.
translations.idiomatic: ----12 Initially, when Emperor Wu destroyed Nanyue, he opened and established Zhuya and Dan'er commanderies on islands in the sea; clerks and soldiers were all men of the central states and often encroached on and bullied the people.

sentences.zh: 其民亦暴惡，自以阻絕，數犯吏禁，率數年壹反，殺吏；

translations.literal: The people too were violent and wicked; trusting themselves cut off by distance, they repeatedly violated official prohibitions—on average once every several years they rebelled and killed officials;
translations.idiomatic: The people too were violent and wicked; trusting themselves cut off by distance, they repeatedly violated official prohibitions—on average once every several years they rebelled and killed officials;

sentences.zh: 漢輒發兵擊定之。

translations.literal: Han would then dispatch troops to attack and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Han would then dispatch troops to attack and pacify them.

sentences.zh: 二十餘年間，凡六反。

translations.literal: Within more than twenty years there were six rebellions in all.
translations.idiomatic: Within more than twenty years there were six rebellions in all.

sentences.zh: 至宣帝時，又再反。

translations.literal: By Emperor Xuan's time they rebelled twice more.
translations.idiomatic: By Emperor Xuan's time they rebelled twice more.

sentences.zh: 上即位之明年，珠崖山南縣反，發兵擊之。

translations.literal: The year after the emperor took the throne, Shannan county in Zhuya rebelled and troops were dispatched to attack it.
translations.idiomatic: The year after the emperor took the throne, Shannan county in Zhuya rebelled and troops were dispatched to attack it.

sentences.zh: 諸縣更叛，連年不定。

translations.literal: The various counties rebelled in turn; for successive years it was not settled.
translations.idiomatic: The various counties rebelled in turn; for successive years it was not settled.

sentences.zh: 上博謀於群臣，欲大發軍。

translations.literal: The emperor broadly deliberated with his ministers and wished to dispatch a great army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor broadly deliberated with his ministers and wished to dispatch a great army.

sentences.zh: 待詔賈捐之曰：「臣聞堯、舜、禹之聖德，地方不過數千里，西被流沙，東漸於海，朔南暨聲教，言欲與聲教則治之，不欲與者不強治也。

translations.literal: Awaiting-edict Jia Juanzhi said: "Your servant has heard that the sage virtue of Yao, Shun, and Yu—their territory did not exceed several thousand li; west it reached the moving sands, east it approached the sea; north and south it extended to their transforming teaching. The saying is: those who wished to receive the transforming teaching were governed; those who did not wish it were not forcibly governed.
translations.idiomatic: Awaiting-edict Jia Juanzhi said, "Your servant has heard that the sage virtue of Yao, Shun, and Yu—their territory did not exceed several thousand li; west it reached the moving sands, east it approached the sea; north and south it extended to their transforming teaching. The saying is: those who wished to receive the transforming teaching were governed; those who did not wish it were not forcibly governed.

sentences.zh: 故君臣歌德，含氣之物各得其宜。

translations.literal: Therefore ruler and ministers sang their virtue, and creatures that breathe each obtained their proper place.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore ruler and ministers sang their virtue, and living creatures each obtained their proper place.

sentences.zh: 武丁、成王，殷、周之大仁也，然地東不過江、黃，西不過氐、羌，南不過蠻荊，北不過朔方，是以頌聲並作，視聽之類鹹樂其生，越裳氏重九譯而獻，此非兵革之所能致也。

translations.literal: Wu Ding and King Cheng were the great benevolence of Yin and Zhou, yet their lands east did not pass the Yangzi and Yellow River, west did not pass the Di and Qiang, south did not pass the southern barbarians and Jing, north did not pass Shuofang—thereby eulogies arose together, and the classes of sight and hearing all rejoiced in their lives; the Yuechang clan, through nine translations, came to offer tribute—this is not what arms and armor could bring about.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ding and King Cheng were the great benevolence of Yin and Zhou, yet their lands east did not pass the Yangzi and Yellow River, west did not pass the Di and Qiang, south did not pass the southern barbarians and Jing, north did not pass Shuofang—thereby eulogies arose together, and all who saw and heard rejoiced in their lives; the Yuechang clan, through nine translations, came to offer tribute—this is not what arms and armor could bring about.

sentences.zh: 以至於秦，興兵遠攻，貪外虛內而天下潰畔。

translations.literal: Reaching Qin, it raised armies for distant attacks, coveting the outer while emptying the inner, and all under Heaven split and turned away.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Qin, it raised armies for distant attacks, coveting the outer while emptying the inner, and the empire split and turned away.

sentences.zh: 孝文皇帝偃武行文，當此之時，斷獄數百，賦役輕簡。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiao Wen laid down arms and promoted culture; at that time cases judged numbered in the hundreds, and levies and corvée were light and simple.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen laid down arms and promoted culture; at that time cases judged numbered in the hundreds, and levies and corvée were light and simple.

sentences.zh: 孝武皇帝厲兵馬以攘四夷，天下斷獄萬數，賦煩役重，寇賊並起，軍旅數發，父戰死於前，子鬥傷於後，女子乘亭障，孤兒號於道，老母、寡婦飲泣巷哭，是皆廓地泰大，征伐不休之故也。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiao Wu sharpened troops and horses to repel the four barbarians; cases judged throughout the empire numbered in the tens of thousands, levies were troublesome and corvée heavy, bandits and robbers arose together, armies were repeatedly dispatched—fathers died in battle ahead, sons were wounded fighting behind, women manned the barrier towers, orphans wailed on the roads, old mothers and widows drank tears and wept in the lanes—all because the territory was vast beyond measure and campaigns and attacks did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu sharpened troops and horses to repel the four barbarians; cases judged throughout the empire numbered in the tens of thousands, levies were troublesome and corvée heavy, bandits and robbers arose together, armies were repeatedly dispatched—fathers died in battle ahead, sons were wounded fighting behind, women manned the barrier towers, orphans wailed on the roads, old mothers and widows wept in the lanes—all because the territory was vast beyond measure and campaigns did not cease.

sentences.zh: 今關東民眾久困，流離道路。

translations.literal: Now the masses east of the Pass have long been distressed, drifting and scattered on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Now the masses east of the Pass have long been distressed, drifting and scattered on the roads.

sentences.zh: 人情莫親父母，莫樂夫婦；

translations.literal: In human feeling none are closer than father and mother, none more joyful than husband and wife;
translations.idiomatic: In human feeling none are closer than father and mother, none more joyful than husband and wife;

sentences.zh: 至嫁妻賣子，法不能禁，義不能止，此社稷之憂也。

translations.literal: yet it has reached selling wives and children—law cannot forbid it, righteousness cannot stop it; this is the state's worry.
translations.idiomatic: yet it has reached selling wives and children—law cannot forbid it, righteousness cannot stop it; this is the state's worry.

sentences.zh: 今陛下不忍悁悁之忿，欲驅士眾擠之大海之中，快心幽冥之地，非所以救助饑饉，保全元元也。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty cannot bear petty anger and wishes to drive soldiers and masses to crowd them into the midst of the great sea, gratifying your heart in a dark and distant land—this is not the way to rescue famine, or preserve the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty cannot bear petty anger and wishes to drive soldiers and masses to crowd them into the midst of the great sea, gratifying your heart in a dark and distant land—this is not the way to rescue famine or preserve the common people.

sentences.zh: 詩云：『蠢爾蠻荊，大邦為讎。

translations.idiomatic: The Odes say, 'Stupid are you, southern barbarians of Jing—the great state becomes your foe.

sentences.zh: 』言聖人起則後服，中國衰則先畔，自古而患之，何況乃復其南方萬里之蠻乎！

translations.literal: ' The saying is: when sages arise they submit afterward; when the central states decline they rebel first—from antiquity this has been a trouble; how much more to recover the southern ten-thousand-li barbarians!

translations.literal: The people of Luoyue bathe father and son in the same stream, are accustomed to drinking through the nose, and differ in nothing from birds and beasts—they originally were not worth establishing commanderies and counties over.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Luoyue bathe father and son in the same stream, are accustomed to drinking through the nose, and differ in nothing from birds and beasts—they originally were not worth establishing commanderies and counties over.

translations.literal: Dull and alone they dwell in the midst of one sea; fog, dew, and damp qi; many poisonous plants, insects, serpents, and harms of water and soil;

sentences.zh: 人未見虜，戰士自死。

translations.literal: before men have seen the enemy, soldiers die on their own.
translations.idiomatic: before men have seen the enemy, soldiers die on their own.

sentences.zh: 又非獨珠崖有珠、犀、玳瑁也。

translations.literal: Moreover it is not that Zhuya alone has pearls, rhinoceros horn, and tortoise shell.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover it is not that Zhuya alone has pearls, rhinoceros horn, and tortoise shell.

sentences.zh: 棄之不足惜，不擊不損威。

translations.literal: To abandon it is not worth regretting; not attacking does not diminish prestige.
translations.idiomatic: To abandon it is not worth regretting; not attacking does not diminish prestige.

sentences.zh: 其民譬猶魚鱉，何足貪也！

translations.literal: Its people are like fish and turtles—what is there worth coveting!
translations.idiomatic: Its people are like fish and turtles—what is there worth coveting!

sentences.zh: 臣竊以往者羌軍言之，暴師曾未一年，兵出不逾千里，費四十餘萬萬；

translations.literal: Your servant privately takes the former Qiang campaign to speak of it: the exposed army had not yet been a year, troops went out not more than a thousand li, and the cost was more than four hundred thousand ten-thousands;
translations.idiomatic: Your servant privately takes the former Qiang campaign to speak of it: the exposed army had not yet been a year, troops went out not more than a thousand li, and the cost was more than four hundred thousand ten-thousands;

sentences.zh: 大司農錢盡，乃以少府禁錢續之。

translations.literal: the Grand Minister of Agriculture's money was exhausted, and then the Privy Treasury's sealed money was used to continue it.
translations.idiomatic: the Grand Minister of Agriculture's money was exhausted, and then the Privy Treasury's sealed money was used to continue it.

sentences.zh: 夫一隅為不善，費尚如此，況於勞師遠攻，亡士毋功乎！

translations.literal: For one corner to be ill-governed the expense was still thus—how much more for tiring the army in distant attack, losing soldiers without achievement!
translations.idiomatic: For one corner to be ill-governed the expense was still thus—how much more for tiring the army in distant attack, losing soldiers without achievement!

sentences.zh: 求之往古則不合，施之當今又不便，臣愚以為非冠帶之國，《禹貢》所及，《春秋》所治，皆可且無以為。

translations.literal: Sought in past antiquity it does not fit; applied in the present it is also not convenient. Your servant is foolish and thinks that for states not of cap and sash, what the Yu Tribute reaches, and what the Spring and Autumn governs—all may for the time being be left undone.

translations.literal: I wish to abandon Zhuya forthwith and devote effort solely to relieving east of the Pass as the worry!
translations.idiomatic: I wish to abandon Zhuya forthwith and devote effort solely to relieving east of the Pass as the worry!

translations.idiomatic: Juanzhi was the great-grandson of Jia Yi.

translations.idiomatic: 1. In spring an edict said, "The barbarians of Zhuya killed officials and people, turned their backs and became rebels.

translations.literal: Now those deliberating at court some say they may be attacked, some say they may be held, some wish to abandon them—their intents each differ.
translations.idiomatic: Now those deliberating at court some say they may be attacked, some say they may be held, some wish to abandon them—their intents each differ.

translations.literal: We day and night only ponder the deliberators' words: if prestige is shamed and not carried out, We wish to execute them;
translations.idiomatic: We day and night only ponder the deliberators' words: if prestige is shamed and not carried out, We wish to execute them;

translations.literal: if We are doubtful and avoid difficulty, then hold them with garrison farming;
translations.idiomatic: if We are doubtful and avoid difficulty, then hold them with garrison farming;

translations.literal: if We penetrate the changes of the times, then We worry for the myriad people.
translations.idiomatic: if We penetrate the changes of the times, then We worry for the myriad people.

sentences.zh: 夫萬民之飢餓與遠蠻之不討，危孰大焉？

translations.literal: Of the myriad people's hunger and the distant barbarians' not being punished—which danger is greater?
translations.idiomatic: Of the myriad people's hunger and the distant barbarians' not being punished—which danger is greater?

sentences.zh: 且宗廟之祭，凶年不備，況乎辟不嫌之辱哉！

translations.literal: Moreover, for the ancestral temple's sacrifices, in famine years they are not complete—how much more to avoid the disgrace one does not despise!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, for the ancestral temple's sacrifices, in famine years they are not complete—how much more to avoid disgrace one does not despise!

sentences.zh: 今關東大困，倉庫空虛，無以相贍，又以動兵，非特勞民，凶年隨之。

translations.literal: Now east of the Pass is greatly distressed, storehouses empty and void, with nothing to support and relieve them; again to move troops—not only does it weary the people, famine years follow.
translations.idiomatic: Now east of the Pass is greatly distressed, storehouses empty and void, with nothing to support and relieve them; again to move troops—not only does it weary the people, famine years follow.

translations.idiomatic: Let Zhuya commandery be abolished; among the people those who admire righteousness and wish to submit inward, conveniently settle them;
