translations.literal: Han deliberated sending Guard Major Gu Ji to escort him; Censor-in-Chief Gong Yu and Erudite Kuang Heng of Donghai held: "Chanyu Zhizhi's turning toward civilization is not yet ripe; his place is utterly remote—it is fitting to have an envoy escort his son only to the passes and then return.
translations.idiomatic: Han deliberated sending Guard Major Gu Ji to escort the prince home; Censor-in-Chief Gong Yu and Erudite Kuang Heng of Donghai argued, "Chanyu Zhizhi's turning toward civilization is not yet secure; his domain is utterly remote—it is fitting to have an envoy escort his son only to the border passes and then return."

sentences.zh: 」吉上書言：「中國與夷狄有羈縻不絕之義，今既養全其子十年，德澤甚厚，空絕而不送，近從塞還，示棄捐不畜，使無鄉從之心，棄前恩，立後怨，不便。

translations.literal: " Ji submitted a memorial, saying: "The Central States and the Yi and Di have the meaning of bridling and tying without breaking off; now that his son has been nourished and kept whole for ten years, virtue's favor is very thick—to cut off empty and not send him, having him return only from near the passes, shows casting away and not keeping him, making him have no heart of homeland to follow, abandoning former grace and establishing later resentment—is not expedient.
translations.idiomatic: " Ji submitted a memorial, saying, "The Central States and the barbarians have the principle of keeping them on loose reins without breaking ties; we have now nourished and kept his son whole for ten years, with very great grace—to cut off ties and not send him home, having him return only from near the passes, shows that we cast him away and will not keep him, leaving him no heart to follow his homeland, abandoning former grace and creating later resentment—is inexpedient."

sentences.zh: 議者見前江乃無應敵之數，智勇俱困，以致恥辱，即豫為臣憂。

translations.literal: The debaters, seeing that earlier Jiang had no means to meet the enemy and both wisdom and courage were exhausted, leading to disgrace, thereby forestall worry for your subject.
translations.idiomatic: The debaters, seeing that Jiang earlier had no means to meet the enemy and that both wisdom and courage were exhausted, leading to disgrace, thereby anticipate worry for your subject.

sentences.zh: 臣幸得建強漢之節，承明聖之詔，宣諭厚恩，不宜敢桀。

translations.literal: Your subject is fortunate to be able to uphold the Han's strong integrity, receive the enlightened sage's edict, proclaim and explain thick grace, and ought not dare to be obstinate.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject is fortunate to uphold the Han's strong integrity, receive the enlightened emperor's edict, proclaim thick grace, and ought not dare to be obstinate.

sentences.zh: 若懷禽獸心，加無道於臣，則單于長嬰大罪，必遁逃遠捨，不敢近邊。

translations.literal: If he harbors a beast's heart and applies injustice to your subject, then the chanyu will long carry a great crime and is sure to flee far and abandon his seat, not daring to approach the border.
translations.idiomatic: If he harbors a beast's heart and does violence to your subject, then the chanyu will long bear a great crime and is sure to flee far away, not daring to approach the border.

sentences.zh: 沒一使以安百姓，國之計，臣之願也。

translations.literal: To lose one envoy to secure the hundred surnames is the state's plan and your subject's wish.
translations.idiomatic: To lose one envoy to secure the common people is the state's plan and your subject's wish.

sentences.zh: 願送至庭。

translations.literal: I wish to escort him to the court.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to escort him to the chanyu's court.

sentences.zh: 」上許焉。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 既到，郅支單于怒，竟殺吉等；

translations.literal: When he had arrived, Chanyu Zhizhi was enraged and in the end killed Ji and the others;
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, Chanyu Zhizhi was enraged and in the end killed Ji and the others;

sentences.zh: 自知負漢，又聞呼韓邪益強，恐見襲擊，欲遠去。

translations.literal: knowing himself to have wronged Han, and also hearing that Huhanye grew daily stronger, he feared being attacked and wished to go far away.
translations.idiomatic: knowing he had wronged Han, and also hearing that Huhanye was growing stronger, he feared attack and wished to go far away.

sentences.zh: 會康居王數為烏孫所困，與諸翕侯計，以為：「匈奴大國，烏孫素服屬之。

translations.literal: It happened that the king of Kangju had repeatedly been distressed by Wusun; with the various xihou he plotted, holding: "The Xiongnu are a great state; Wusun has long submitted and belonged to them.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that the king of Kangju had repeatedly been harassed by Wusun; with the various chieftains he plotted, saying, "The Xiongnu are a great power; Wusun has long submitted to them."

sentences.zh: 今郅支單于困厄在外，可迎置東邊，使合兵取烏孫而立之，長無匈奴憂矣。

translations.literal: Now Chanyu Zhizhi is distressed and stranded abroad; we can welcome and place him on the east, make him combine troops to take Wusun and establish him—then there will long be no Xiongnu worry.
translations.idiomatic: Now Chanyu Zhizhi is distressed and stranded abroad; we can welcome him and place him in the east, combine forces to take Wusun and establish him there—then we will long be free of Xiongnu trouble."

sentences.zh: 」即使使到堅昆，通語郅支。

translations.literal: " They thereupon sent an envoy to Jiankun to communicate with Zhizhi.
translations.idiomatic: " They thereupon sent an envoy to Jiankun to communicate with Zhizhi.

sentences.zh: 郅支素恐，又怨烏孫，聞康居計，大說，遂與相結，引兵而西。

translations.literal: Zhizhi had long been fearful and again resented Wusun; hearing Kangju's plan, he was greatly pleased, thereupon joined with them, and led his troops west.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhi had long been fearful and resented Wusun; hearing Kangju's plan, he was greatly pleased, joined with them, and led his troops west.

sentences.zh: 郅支人眾中寒道死，餘財三千人。

translations.literal: Among Zhizhi's masses many died on the road from cold; only about three thousand remained.
translations.idiomatic: Many of Zhizhi's followers died on the road from cold; only about three thousand remained.

sentences.zh: 到康居，康居王以女妻郅支，郅支亦以女予康居王，康居甚尊敬郅支，欲倚其威以脅諸國。

translations.literal: When he reached Kangju, the king of Kangju gave his daughter in marriage to Zhizhi; Zhizhi also gave his daughter to the king of Kangju; Kangju greatly honored Zhizhi, wishing to rely on his might to coerce the various states.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Kangju, the king of Kangju gave his daughter in marriage to Zhizhi; Zhizhi also gave his daughter to the king of Kangju; Kangju greatly honored Zhizhi, wishing to rely on his might to intimidate the various states.

sentences.zh: 郅支數借兵擊烏孫，深入至谷城，殺略民人，驅畜產去。

translations.literal: Zhizhi repeatedly borrowed troops to attack Wusun, penetrating deep to Valley City, killing and plundering the people, and driving off livestock.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhi repeatedly borrowed troops to attack Wusun, penetrating deep to Valley City, killing and plundering the people, and driving off livestock.

sentences.zh: 烏孫不敢追。

translations.literal: Wusun did not dare pursue.
translations.idiomatic: Wusun did not dare pursue.

sentences.zh: 西邊空虛不居者五千里。

translations.literal: The western border lay empty and uninhabited for five thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: The western border lay empty and uninhabited for five thousand li.

sentences.zh: ----7冬，十二月，丁末，貢禹卒。

translations.literal: ----7 In winter, the twelfth month, on day dingmo, Gong Yu died.
translations.idiomatic: ----7 In winter, the twelfth month, on day dingmo, Gong Yu died.

sentences.zh: 丁已，長信少府薛廣德為御史大夫。

translations.literal: On day dingsi, Chief Steward for Eternal Faith Xue Guangde became censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: On day dingsi, Chief Steward for Eternal Faith Xue Guangde became censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，上行幸甘泉，郊泰畤。

translations.literal: 1 In spring, the first month, the emperor traveled in favor to Sweet Springs and sacrificed at the Great Altar.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In spring, the first month, the emperor traveled to Sweet Springs and sacrificed at the Great Altar.

sentences.zh: 視畢，因留射獵。

translations.literal: When the rites were finished, he thereupon remained to shoot and hunt.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were finished, he remained to hunt.

sentences.zh: 薛廣德上書曰：「竊見關東困極，人民流離。

translations.literal: Xue Guangde submitted a memorial, saying: "I have seen that east of the passes is extremely distressed and the people are displaced and adrift.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Guangde submitted a memorial, saying, "I have seen that east of the passes is in extreme distress and the people are displaced."

sentences.zh: 陛下日撞亡秦之鐘，聽鄭、衛之樂，臣誠悼之。

translations.literal: Your Majesty daily strikes Qin's bell of ruin and listens to Zheng and Wei's music—your subject is truly grieved.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty daily strikes Qin's bell of ruin and listens to Zheng and Wei music—your subject is truly grieved."

sentences.zh: 今士卒暴露，從官勞倦，願陛下亟反宮，思與百姓同憂樂，天下幸甚！

translations.literal: Now soldiers stand exposed and attending officials are weary with labor; I wish Your Majesty would quickly return to the palace and think to share worry and joy with the hundred surnames—the realm would be greatly fortunate!
translations.idiomatic: Now soldiers stand exposed and attending officials are weary; I wish Your Majesty would quickly return to the palace and think to share worry and joy with the people—the realm would be greatly fortunate!"

sentences.zh: 」上即日還。

translations.literal: " The emperor returned that same day.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor returned that same day.

sentences.zh: ----2二月，詔：「丞相、御史舉質樸、敦厚、遜讓、有行者，光祿歲以此科第郎、從官。

translations.literal: ----2 In the second month, an edict: "The chancellor and censor are to recommend men who are plain, sincere, humble, yielding, and of conduct; the Director of the Masters of Writing each year is to rank palace gentlemen and attendants by this category.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 In the second month, an edict: "The chancellor and censor are to recommend men who are plain, sincere, humble, yielding, and of good conduct; the Director of the Masters of Writing each year is to rank palace gentlemen and attendants by this standard."

translations.literal: " ----3 In the third month, he amnestied All-under-Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: " ----3 In the third month, he amnestied All-under-Heaven.

sentences.zh: ----4雨雪、隕霜，殺桑。

translations.literal: ----4 Rain and snow fell, frost dropped from the sky, and mulberry trees were killed.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 Rain and snow fell, frost dropped from the sky, and mulberry trees were killed.

sentences.zh: ----5秋，上酎祭宗廟，出便門，欲御樓船。

translations.literal: ----5 In autumn, the emperor performed the autumnal offering sacrifice at the ancestral temples, went out through Convenience Gate, and wished to ride a tower boat.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 In autumn, the emperor performed the autumnal offering at the ancestral temples, went out through Convenience Gate, and wished to ride a tower boat.

sentences.zh: 薛廣德當乘輿車，免冠頓首曰：「宜從橋。

translations.literal: Xue Guangde was to attend the imperial carriage, removed his cap and knocked his head, saying: "You ought to go by the bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Guangde was to attend the imperial carriage, removed his cap and knocked his head, saying, "You ought to go by the bridge."

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「大夫冠。

translations.literal: " An edict said: "Grandee, put on your cap.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict said, "Grandee, put on your cap."

sentences.zh: 」廣德曰：「陛下不聽臣，臣自刎，以血污車輪，陛下不得入廟矣！

translations.literal: " Guangde said: "If Your Majesty will not heed your subject, your subject will cut his own throat and stain the carriage wheels with blood—Your Majesty will not be able to enter the temple!
translations.idiomatic: " Guangde said, "If Your Majesty will not heed your subject, your subject will cut his own throat and stain the carriage wheels with blood—Your Majesty will not be able to enter the temple!"

sentences.zh: 」上不說。

translations.literal: " The emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 先驅光祿大夫張猛進曰：「臣聞主聖臣直。

translations.literal: The vanguard Director of the Masters of Writing Zhang Meng advanced and said: "Your subject has heard that when the ruler is sage, ministers are upright.
translations.idiomatic: The vanguard Director of the Masters of Writing Zhang Meng advanced and said, "Your subject has heard that when the ruler is sage, ministers are upright."

sentences.zh: 乘船危，就橋安，聖主不乘危。

translations.literal: Riding a boat is perilous; taking the bridge is secure—a sage ruler does not ride peril.
translations.idiomatic: Riding a boat is perilous; taking the bridge is secure—a sage ruler does not court peril."

sentences.zh: 御史大夫言可聽。

translations.literal: The censor-in-chief's words may be heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The censor-in-chief's words should be heeded."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「曉人不當如是邪！

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Should not one who understands people be like this!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Should not one who understands people be like this!"

sentences.zh: 」乃從橋。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he went by the bridge.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he went by the bridge.

sentences.zh: ----6九月，隕霜殺稼，天下大饑。

translations.literal: ----6 In the ninth month, frost dropped from the sky and killed the grain crops; All-under-Heaven suffered great famine.
translations.idiomatic: ----6 In the ninth month, frost dropped from the sky and killed the crops; the realm suffered great famine.

sentences.zh: 丞相-{于定國}-，大司馬、車騎將軍史高，御史大夫薛廣德，俱以災異乞骸骨。

translations.literal: Chancellor -{Yu Dingguo}-, Grand Marshal and General of Chariots and Cavalry Shi Gao, and Censor-in-Chief Xue Guangde all requested their bones on account of prodigies and anomalies.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor -{Yu Dingguo}-, Grand Marshal and General of Chariots and Cavalry Shi Gao, and Censor-in-Chief Xue Guangde all resigned on account of prodigies and anomalies.

sentences.zh: 賜安車、駟馬、黃金六十斤，罷。

translations.literal: They were granted cushioned carriages, four-horse teams, and sixty jin of gold, and were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: They were granted cushioned carriages, four-horse teams, and sixty jin of gold, and were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 太子太傅韋玄成為御史大夫。

translations.literal: Tutor of the Heir Apparent Wei Xuancheng became censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Tutor of the Heir Apparent Wei Xuancheng became censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 廣德歸，縣其安車，以傳示子孫為榮。

translations.literal: Guangde returned home and displayed his cushioned carriage, transmitting it to show his sons and grandsons as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Guangde returned home and displayed his cushioned carriage, passing it down to show his descendants as an honor.

sentences.zh: ----7帝之為太子也，從太中大夫孔霸受《尚書》。

translations.literal: ----7 When the emperor was heir apparent, he followed Grand Master of the Palace Kong Ba in receiving the Documents.
translations.idiomatic: ----7 When the emperor was heir apparent, he studied the Documents under Grand Master of the Palace Kong Ba.

sentences.zh: 及即位，賜霸爵關內侯，號褒成君，給事中。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, he granted Ba the rank of marquis within the passes, styled him Lord of Baocheng, and made him attendant within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne, he granted Ba the rank of marquis within the passes, styled him Lord of Baocheng, and made him attendant within the palace.

sentences.zh: 上欲致霸相位，霸為人謙退，不好權勢，常稱「爵位泰過，何德以堪之！

translations.literal: The emperor wished to elevate Ba to chancellor rank; Ba was by nature humble and retiring, not fond of power and influence, and often said: "My noble rank is too excessive—what virtue could bear it!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to elevate Ba to chancellor; Ba was humble and retiring, not fond of power, and often said, "My noble rank is too high—what virtue could bear it!"

sentences.zh: 」御史大夫屢缺，上輒欲用霸；

translations.literal: " The office of censor-in-chief was repeatedly vacant, and the emperor would then wish to employ Ba;
translations.idiomatic: " The office of censor-in-chief was repeatedly vacant, and the emperor would then wish to employ Ba;

sentences.zh: 霸讓位，自陳至於再三。

translations.literal: Ba yielded the post and stated his reasons again and again.
translations.idiomatic: Ba yielded the post and stated his reasons repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 上深知其至誠，乃弗用。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply knew his utmost sincerity and therefore did not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply knew his utmost sincerity and therefore did not employ him.

sentences.zh: 以是敬之，賞賜甚厚。

translations.literal: Because of this the emperor honored him and bestowed rewards very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this the emperor honored him and bestowed very generous rewards.

sentences.zh: ----8戊子，侍中，衛尉王接為大司馬、車騎將軍。

translations.literal: ----8 On day wuzi, Attendant within the Palace and Commandant of the Guards Wang Jie became grand marshal and general of chariots and cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: ----8 On day wuzi, Attendant within the Palace and Commandant of the Guards Wang Jie became grand marshal and general of chariots and cavalry.

sentences.zh: ----9石顯憚周堪、張猛等，數譖毀之。

translations.literal: ----9 Shi Xian feared Zhou Kan, Zhang Meng, and others, and repeatedly slandered and defamed them.
translations.idiomatic: ----9 Shi Xian feared Zhou Kan, Zhang Meng, and others, and repeatedly slandered them.

sentences.zh: 劉更生懼其傾危，上書曰：「臣聞舜命九官，濟濟相讓，和之至也。

translations.literal: Liu Gengsheng feared they would be overturned and submitted a memorial, saying: "Your subject has heard that when Shun appointed the nine officers, they yielded to one another in abundance—this was harmony at its height.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gengsheng feared they would be overthrown and submitted a memorial, saying, "Your subject has heard that when Shun appointed the nine officers, they yielded to one another in abundance—this was harmony at its height."

sentences.zh: 眾臣和於朝則萬物和於野，故簫《韶》九成，鳳皇來儀。

translations.literal: When the multitude of ministers were harmonious at court, then the myriad things were harmonious in the wilds; therefore when the Xiao Shao was played nine times, the phoenix came to take its place.
translations.idiomatic: When ministers were harmonious at court, the myriad things were harmonious in the wilds; therefore when the Xiao Shao was played nine times, the phoenix came to take its place."

sentences.zh: 至周幽，厲之際，朝廷不和，轉相非怨，則日月薄食，水泉沸騰，山谷易處，霜降失節。

translations.literal: Down to the time of King You and King Li of Zhou, when the court was not harmonious and ministers turned to blame and resent one another, then sun and moon were eclipsed, springs boiled over, valleys changed their places, and frost fell out of season.
translations.idiomatic: Down to the time of Kings You and Li of Zhou, when the court was not harmonious and ministers turned to blame and resent one another, sun and moon were eclipsed, springs boiled over, valleys shifted, and frost fell out of season."

sentences.zh: 由此觀之，和氣致祥，乖氣致異，祥多者其國安，異眾者其國危。

translations.literal: Viewed from this, harmonious qi brings auspice, perverse qi brings prodigies; where auspices are many the state is secure, where prodigies are many the state is perilous.
translations.idiomatic: Viewed from this, harmonious qi brings auspice, perverse qi brings prodigies; where auspices are many the state is secure, where prodigies are many the state is in peril."

sentences.zh: 天地之常經，古今之通義也。

translations.literal: This is Heaven and Earth's constant canon and the common meaning through antiquity and the present.
translations.idiomatic: This is Heaven and Earth's constant canon and the common meaning through antiquity and the present."

sentences.zh: 今陛下開三代之業，招文學之士，優遊寬容，使得並進。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty has opened the enterprise of the Three Dynasties, summoned men of letters, and been leisurely, lenient, and tolerant, enabling them to advance together.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty has opened the enterprise of the Three Dynasties, summoned men of letters, and been leisurely, lenient, and tolerant, enabling them to advance together."

sentences.zh: 今賢不肖渾殽，白黑不分，邪正雜糅，忠讒並進；

translations.literal: Yet now worthy and unworthy are mixed in confusion, white and black are not distinguished, crooked and straight are intermingled, and loyal and slanderous advance together;
translations.idiomatic: Yet now worthy and unworthy are mixed in confusion, right and wrong are not distinguished, crooked and straight are intermingled, and loyal and slanderous men advance together;"

sentences.zh: 章交公車，人滿北軍，朝臣舛午，膠戾乖剌，更相讒訴，轉相是非；

translations.literal: memorials crowd the imperial carriage office, men fill the Northern Army, court ministers clash at noon, stick fast in perversity and cut against one another, alternately slander and accuse, and turn to judge right and wrong;
translations.idiomatic: memorials crowd the imperial carriage office, men fill the Northern Army, court ministers clash, stick fast in perversity and cut against one another, alternately slander and accuse, and turn to judge right and wrong;"

sentences.zh: 所以營惑耳目，感移心意，不可勝載，分曹為黨，往往群朋將同心以陷正臣。

translations.literal: thereby bewildering ears and eyes, moving and shifting the heart's intent—more than can be recorded; they divide into bureaus and form factions, often banding together to join hearts and entrap upright ministers.
translations.idiomatic: thereby bewildering ears and eyes and shifting the heart's intent—more than can be recorded; they divide into factions and often band together to entrap upright ministers."

sentences.zh: 正臣進者，治之表也；

translations.literal: When upright ministers advance, it is the outward sign of good governance;
translations.idiomatic: When upright ministers advance, it is the outward sign of good governance;"

sentences.zh: 正臣陷者，亂之機也；

translations.literal: when upright ministers are entrapped, it is the mechanism of disorder;
translations.idiomatic: when upright ministers are entrapped, it is the mechanism of disorder;"

sentences.zh: 乘治亂之機，未知孰任，而災異數見，此臣所以寒心者也。

translations.literal: seizing the mechanism between order and disorder, not knowing who will bear responsibility, while prodigies and anomalies repeatedly appear—this is why your subject's heart is chilled.
translations.idiomatic: seizing the mechanism between order and disorder, not knowing who will bear responsibility, while prodigies and anomalies repeatedly appear—this is why your subject's heart is chilled."

sentences.zh: 初元以來六年矣，按春秋六年之中，災異未有稠如今者也。

translations.literal: Six years have passed since the beginning of Chuyuan; examining the Spring and Autumn Annals' six-year spans, prodigies and anomalies have never been as dense as now.
translations.idiomatic: Six years have passed since the beginning of Chuyuan; examining six-year spans in the Spring and Autumn Annals, prodigies and anomalies have never been as dense as now."

sentences.zh: 原其所以然者，由讒邪並進也；

translations.literal: Tracing why it is so, it is because slander and wickedness advance together;
translations.idiomatic: Tracing why it is so, it is because slander and wickedness advance together;"

sentences.zh: 讒邪之所以並進者，由上多疑心，既已用賢人而行善政，如或譖之，則賢人退而善政還矣。

translations.literal: the reason slander and wickedness advance together is that above there is much doubting heart; having already employed worthy men and practiced good government, if someone slanders them, then worthy men withdraw and good government returns.
translations.idiomatic: the reason slander and wickedness advance together is that above there is much doubting; having already employed worthy men and practiced good government, if someone slanders them, worthy men withdraw and good government is undone."

sentences.zh: 夫執狐疑之心者，來讒賊之口；

translations.literal: One who holds a fox-doubting heart invites the mouths of slanderous villains;
translations.idiomatic: One who holds a doubting heart invites slanderous mouths;"

sentences.zh: 持不斷之意者，開群枉之門；

translations.literal: one who maintains an undecisive intent opens the gate for a crowd of crooked men;
translations.idiomatic: one who maintains an undecisive intent opens the gate for a crowd of crooked men;"

sentences.zh: 讒邪進則眾賢退，群枉盛則正士消。

translations.literal: when slander and wickedness advance, the multitude of worthies withdraw; when the crowd of crooked men flourishes, upright gentlemen vanish.
translations.idiomatic: when slander and wickedness advance, the multitude of worthies withdraw; when crooked men flourish, upright gentlemen vanish."

sentences.zh: 故《易》有《否》、《泰》，小人道長，君子道消，則政日亂；

translations.literal: Therefore the Changes has Pi and Tai: when the petty man's Way grows long and the gentleman's Way wanes, government daily grows disordered;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Changes has Pi and Tai: when the petty man's way grows long and the gentleman's way wanes, government daily grows disordered;"

sentences.zh: 君子道長，小人道消，則政日治。

translations.literal: when the gentleman's Way grows long and the petty man's Way wanes, government daily grows well ordered.
translations.idiomatic: when the gentleman's way grows long and the petty man's way wanes, government daily grows well ordered."

sentences.zh: 昔者鯀、共工、驩兜與舜、禹雜處堯朝，周公與管、蔡並居周位，當是時，迭進相毀，流言相謗，豈可勝道哉！

translations.literal: In antiquity Gun, Gong Gong, and Huan Dou were mixed in Yao's court with Shun and Yu; the Duke of Zhou and Guan and Cai together held Zhou offices—at that time they advanced in turn to destroy one another and floating words slandered one another—how could it all be told!
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Gun, Gong Gong, and Huan Dou were mixed in Yao's court with Shun and Yu; the Duke of Zhou and Guan and Cai together held Zhou offices—at that time they advanced in turn to destroy one another and rumors slandered one another—how could it all be told!"

sentences.zh: 帝堯、成王能賢舜、禹、周公而消共工、管、蔡，故以大治，榮華至今。

translations.literal: Emperors Yao and King Cheng were able to treat Shun, Yu, and the Duke of Zhou as worthy and eliminate Gong Gong, Guan, and Cai; therefore there was great order and glory and splendor down to the present.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors Yao and King Cheng were able to treat Shun, Yu, and the Duke of Zhou as worthy and eliminate Gong Gong, Guan, and Cai; therefore there was great order and glory down to the present."

sentences.zh: 孔子與季、孟偕仕於魯，李斯與叔孫俱宦於秦，定公、始皇賢季、孟、李斯而消孔子、叔孫，故以大亂，污辱至今。

translations.literal: Confucius served in Lu together with the Ji and Meng clans; Li Si and Shusun both held office in Qin; Duke Ding and the First Emperor treated the Ji, Meng, and Li Si as worthy and eliminated Confucius and Shusun—therefore there was great disorder and filth and disgrace down to the present.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius served in Lu together with the Ji and Meng clans; Li Si and Shusun both held office in Qin; Duke Ding and the First Emperor treated the Ji, Meng, and Li Si as worthy and eliminated Confucius and Shusun—therefore there was great disorder and disgrace down to the present."

sentences.zh: 故治亂榮辱之端，在所信任；

translations.literal: Therefore the beginning of order and disorder, glory and disgrace, lies in whom one trusts;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the beginning of order and disorder, glory and disgrace, lies in whom one trusts;"

sentences.zh: 信任既賢，在於堅固而不移。

translations.literal: once trust is placed in the worthy, it lies in being firm and not shifting.
translations.idiomatic: once trust is placed in the worthy, it lies in being firm and not shifting."

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：『我心匪石，不可轉也，言守善篤也。

translations.literal: The Odes says: 'My heart is not stone—it cannot be turned,' speaking of steadfastly keeping to the good.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes says, "My heart is not stone—it cannot be turned," speaking of steadfastly keeping to the good."

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：『渙汗其大號』，言號令如汗，汗出而不反者也。

translations.literal: The Changes says: 'He disperses sweat with his great proclamation,' meaning that orders are like sweat—once sweat issues forth it does not return.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says, "He disperses sweat with his great proclamation," meaning that orders are like sweat—once sweat issues forth it does not return."

sentences.zh: 今出善令未能逾時而反，是反汗也；

translations.literal: Now good orders are issued but cannot pass the season before being reversed—this is reversing sweat;
translations.idiomatic: Now good orders are issued but cannot pass the season before being reversed—this is reversing sweat;"

sentences.zh: 用賢未能三旬而退，是轉石也。

translations.literal: employing the worthy but not reaching thirty days before dismissing them—this is turning stone.
translations.idiomatic: employing the worthy but not reaching thirty days before dismissing them—this is turning stone."

sentences.zh: 《論語》曰：『見不善如探湯。

translations.literal: The Analects says: 'Seeing what is not good is like probing boiling water.'
translations.idiomatic: The Analects says, "Seeing what is not good is like probing boiling water."

sentences.zh: 』今二府奏佞謅不當在位，歷年而不去。

translations.literal: ' Now the Two Offices memorialize that flatterers and sycophants ought not to hold office, yet year after year they are not removed.
translations.idiomatic: " Now the Two Offices memorialize that flatterers and sycophants ought not to hold office, yet year after year they are not removed."

sentences.zh: 故出令則如反汗，用賢則如轉石，去佞則如撥山，如此，望陰陽之調，不亦難乎！

translations.literal: Therefore issuing orders is like reversing sweat, employing the worthy is like turning stone, removing flatterers is like moving mountains—with this, to hope for the harmony of yin and yang—is it not difficult!
translations.idiomatic: Therefore issuing orders is like reversing sweat, employing the worthy is like turning stone, removing flatterers is like moving mountains—with this, to hope for the harmony of yin and yang—is it not difficult!"

sentences.zh: 是以群小窺見間隙，緣飾文字，巧言醜詆，流言、飛文嘩於民間。

translations.literal: Because of this the crowd of petty men spy out gaps, trim and adorn their words, use clever speech to defame uglily, and floating words and flying writings clamor among the people.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this petty men spy out gaps, trim and adorn their words, use clever speech to defame, and rumors and flying writings clamor among the people."

sentences.zh: 故《詩》云：『憂心悄悄，慍於群小，』小人成群，誠足慍也。

translations.literal: Therefore the Odes says: 'My worried heart is secret, angry at the crowd of petty men'—when petty men form crowds, it is truly enough to anger one.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Odes says, "My worried heart is secret, angry at the crowd of petty men"—when petty men form crowds, it is truly enough to anger one."

sentences.zh: 昔孔子與顏淵、子貢更相稱譽，不為朋黨；

translations.literal: In antiquity Confucius with Yan Yuan and Zigong praised one another in turn and did not form factions;
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Confucius with Yan Yuan and Zigong praised one another in turn and did not form factions;"

sentences.zh: 禹、稷與皋陶傳相汲引，不為比周，何則？

translations.literal: Yu and Ji with Gao Yao passed on and drew one another up and did not form cliquish alliances—why was it so?
translations.idiomatic: Yu and Ji with Gao Yao passed on and drew one another up and did not form cliquish alliances—why was it so?

sentences.zh: 忠於為國，無邪心也。

translations.literal: Loyal in serving the state, without a wicked heart.
translations.idiomatic: They were loyal in serving the state, without wicked intent.

sentences.zh: 今佞邪與賢臣並交戟之內，合黨共謀，違善依惡，歙歙訿訿，數設危險之言，欲以傾移主上，如忽然用之，此天地之所以先戒，災異之所以重至者也。

translations.literal: Now the sycophantic and wicked and worthy ministers together within crossed halberds, join factions and plot together, turn from good and rely on evil, whisper and clamor, repeatedly set forth dangerous words, wishing thereby to overturn and shift the sovereign—if suddenly employed, this is why Heaven and Earth give prior warnings and why calamities and anomalies repeatedly arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Now the sycophantic and wicked mingle with worthy ministers in the same court, form factions and plot together, turn from good and rely on evil, whisper and clamor, and repeatedly utter dangerous words, wishing to sway the sovereign. If such men were suddenly put in power, that is why Heaven and Earth give warnings beforehand and why calamities and portents come again and again.

sentences.zh: 自古明聖未有無誅而治者也，故舜有四放之罰，孔子有兩觀之誅，然後聖化可得而行也。

translations.literal: From antiquity enlightened sages have never governed without executions; therefore Shun had the punishment of four banishments, Confucius had the execution at the two watchtowers—only then could sage transformation be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity no enlightened sage has ever governed without punishments. Shun had the four banishments, and Confucius had the execution at the two watchtowers—only then could sage transformation be carried out.

sentences.zh: 今以陛下明知，誠深思天地之心，覽《否》、《泰》之卦，歷周、唐之所進以為法，原秦、魯之所消以為戒，考祥應之福、災異之禍，以揆當世之變，放遠佞邪之黨，壞散險詖之聚，杜閉群枉之門，廣開眾正之路，決斷狐疑，分別猶豫，便是非炳然可知，則百異消滅而眾祥並至，太平之基，萬世之利也。

translations.literal: Now with Your Majesty's clear understanding, truly deeply ponder Heaven and Earth's heart, review the hexagrams Pi and Tai, pass through what Zhou and Tang advanced and take it as model, trace what Qin and Lu consumed away and take it as warning, examine the blessings of auspicious responses and the disasters of calamities and anomalies to measure the changes of the present age, release and send far the faction of sycophants and the wicked, break up and scatter gatherings of dangerous slander, shut and close the gates of many perversities, broadly open the road of the multitude of the upright, decisively cut off doubt, distinguish hesitation—then right and wrong will be brilliantly clear and knowable; then the hundred anomalies will vanish and the many auspicious signs will arrive together—the foundation of great peace, the benefit of ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Now, with Your Majesty's clear understanding, truly ponder Heaven and Earth's intent, study the hexagrams Pi and Tai, take what Zhou and Tang advanced as your model and what Qin and Lu destroyed themselves by as your warning, weigh the blessings of auspicious omens against the disasters of portents to gauge the changes of the age, banish the faction of sycophants and the wicked, break up gatherings of dangerous slander, shut the gates of perversity, and open wide the path of the upright. Cut through doubt and distinguish what is uncertain, so that right and wrong stand clear; then the hundred anomalies will vanish, many auspicious signs will come together, and the foundation of great peace and the benefit of ten thousand generations will be secured.

sentences.zh: 」顯見其書，愈與許、史比而怨更生等。

translations.literal: " Xian saw his memorial and all the more aligned with Xu and Shi while resenting Gengsheng and the others.
translations.idiomatic: " When Xian saw the memorial, he drew still closer to Xu and Shi and bore resentment toward Gengsheng and his associates.

sentences.zh: 是歲，夏寒，日青無光，顯及許、史皆言堪、猛用事之咎。

translations.literal: That year, summer was cold; the sun was greenish and without light; Xian and Xu and Shi all said it was the fault of Kan and Meng holding power.
translations.idiomatic: That year summer was cold, the sun looked greenish and dim, and Xian together with Xu and Shi all said it was because Kan and Meng were wielding power.

sentences.zh: 上內重堪，又患眾口之浸潤，無所取信。

translations.literal: The emperor inwardly valued Kan highly, yet also worried at the soaking infiltration of many mouths, with nothing by which to take faith.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor inwardly valued Kan highly, yet also worried that constant slander from many quarters left him nothing he could trust.

sentences.zh: 時長安令楊興以材能幸，常稱譽堪，上欲以為助，乃見問興：「朝臣斷斷不可光祿勳，何邪？

translations.literal: At the time Metropolitan Magistrate Yang Xing, favored for talent and ability, often praised Kan; the emperor wished to use him as help and therefore summoned and asked Xing: "The court ministers insistently say the Grand Master of Splendor cannot serve—why?
translations.idiomatic: At the time Metropolitan Magistrate Yang Xing, favored for his talent, often praised Kan. The emperor wished to use him as an ally and therefore summoned Xing and asked, "The court ministers keep insisting that the Grand Master of Splendor cannot serve—why is that?

sentences.zh: 」興者，傾巧士，謂上疑堪，因順指曰：「堪非獨不可於朝廷，自-{州里}-亦不可也！

translations.literal: " Xing was a crafty, leaning sort of man; thinking the emperor doubted Kan, he therefore followed the thrust and said: "Kan is not only unfit at court—even in his own -{州里}- he is unfit!
translations.idiomatic: " Xing was a crafty opportunist. Seeing that the emperor doubted Kan, he followed the emperor's inclination and said, "Kan is not only unfit at court—even in his own -{州里}- he is unfit!"

sentences.zh: 臣見眾人聞堪與劉更生等謀毀骨肉，以為當誅；

translations.literal: Your subject has seen that when the multitude heard Kan and Liu Gengsheng and others plotted to destroy flesh-and-bone kin, they thought he ought to be executed;
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has seen that when people heard Kan and Liu Gengsheng and others were plotting to harm the emperor's own kin, they thought he ought to be executed;

sentences.zh: 故臣前書言堪不可誅傷，為國養恩也。

translations.literal: therefore your subject in a former memorial said Kan ought not be executed or harmed—it was to nurture grace for the state.
translations.idiomatic: therefore your subject wrote earlier that Kan ought not be executed or harmed, in order to preserve grace for the state.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「然此何罪而誅？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Yet what crime is this for execution?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Yet what crime would justify execution?

sentences.zh: 今宜奈何？

translations.literal: What ought be done now?
translations.idiomatic: What should be done now?

sentences.zh: 」興曰：「臣愚以為可賜爵關內侯，食邑三百戶，勿令典事。

translations.literal: " Xing said: "Your subject foolishly thinks he may be granted rank as Marquis within the Passes, with a fief of three hundred households, and not be allowed to handle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " Xing said, "Your subject foolishly thinks he might be granted rank as Marquis within the Passes, with a fief of three hundred households, and not be allowed to handle affairs.

sentences.zh: 明主不失師傅之恩，此最策之得者也。

translations.literal: An enlightened ruler does not lose the grace owed a teacher—this is the most successful policy.
translations.idiomatic: An enlightened ruler does not cast off the grace owed a teacher—this is the best possible policy.

sentences.zh: 」上於是疑之。

translations.literal: " The emperor thereupon came to doubt him.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor thereupon came to doubt Kan.

sentences.zh: 司隸校尉琅邪諸葛豐始以特立剛直著名於朝，數侵犯貴戚，在位多言其短。

translations.literal: Director of Convict Labor Zhuge Feng of Langye was at first famed in court for standing alone and being sternly upright; he repeatedly encroached on noble kin, and those in office often spoke of his faults.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Convict Labor Zhuge Feng of Langye was at first famed at court for his uncompromising integrity; he repeatedly clashed with powerful families, and those in office often spoke of his faults.

sentences.zh: 後坐春夏系治人，徙城門校尉。

translations.literal: Later he was convicted for imprisoning and prosecuting people in spring and summer and was transferred to be Commandant of the City Gates.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was convicted for imprisoning and prosecuting people in spring and summer and was transferred to Commandant of the City Gates.

sentences.zh: 豐於是上書告堪、猛罪，上不直豐，乃制詔御史：「城門校尉豐，前與光祿勳、光祿大夫猛在朝之時，數稱言堪、猛之美。

translations.literal: Feng thereupon submitted a memorial accusing Kan and Meng of crimes; the emperor did not side with Feng and therefore issued an edict to the imperial censor: "Commandant of the City Gates Feng, when formerly together with the Grand Master of Splendor and Grand Master of the Palace Meng at court, repeatedly spoke of Kan and Meng's excellence.
translations.idiomatic: Feng thereupon submitted a memorial accusing Kan and Meng of crimes. The emperor did not side with Feng and issued an edict to the imperial censor: "Commandant of the City Gates Feng, when he was at court with the Grand Master of Splendor and Grand Master of the Palace Meng, repeatedly praised Kan and Meng.

sentences.zh: 豐前為司隸校尉，不順四時，修法度，專作苛暴以獲虛威；

translations.literal: Feng formerly as Director of Convict Labor did not follow the four seasons, revised laws and standards, and exclusively made harsh cruelty to obtain empty prestige;
translations.idiomatic: When Feng was Director of Convict Labor he ignored the seasons, revised laws and standards, and relied on harsh cruelty to win empty prestige;

sentences.zh: 朕不忍下吏，以為城門校尉。

translations.literal: We could not bear to send him down to the officials and made him Commandant of the City Gates.
translations.idiomatic: We could not bear to hand him over to the law officers and made him Commandant of the City Gates instead.

sentences.zh: 不內省諸己，而反怨堪、猛以求報舉，告按無證之辭，暴揚難驗之罪，毀譽恣意，不顧前言，不信之大也。

translations.literal: He does not inwardly examine himself, yet on the contrary resents Kan and Meng to seek retaliation and impeachment, reporting and prosecuting words without evidence, openly displaying crimes hard to verify, praise and blame as he pleases, not looking to his former words—great untrustworthiness.
translations.idiomatic: He does not examine himself, yet resents Kan and Meng and seeks retaliation, lodging accusations without evidence and publicly airing charges hard to prove, praising and blaming as he pleases without regard to his former words—this is gross faithlessness.

sentences.zh: 朕憐豐之耆老，不忍加刑，其免為庶人！

translations.literal: We pity Feng's old age and cannot bear to add punishment; let him be dismissed as a commoner!
translations.idiomatic: We pity Feng in his old age and cannot bear to punish him further; let him be dismissed as a commoner!"

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「豐言堪、猛貞信不立，朕閔而不治，又惜其材能未有所效，其左遷堪為河東太守，猛槐里令。

translations.literal: " He also said: "Feng said Kan and Meng's uprightness and trustworthiness were not established; We pitied them and did not prosecute, yet also cherished that their talent and ability had not yet shown effect—let Kan be demoted to Administrator of Hedong, and Meng Magistrate of Huaili.
translations.idiomatic: " He also said, "Feng claimed Kan and Meng lacked integrity; We pitied them and did not prosecute, yet also regretted that their talents had not yet borne fruit—demote Kan to Administrator of Hedong and Meng to Magistrate of Huaili."

sentences.zh: :臣光曰：諸葛豐之於堪、猛，前譽而後毀，其志非為朝廷進善而去奸也，欲比周求進而已矣。

translations.literal: : Minister Guang said: Zhuge Feng toward Kan and Meng—first praising, afterward destroying—the intent was not to advance good for the court and remove wickedness; he wished only to form cliques and seek advancement.
translations.idiomatic: : Minister Guang said: Zhuge Feng toward Kan and Meng praised them first and slandered them afterward. His aim was not to advance good for the court and remove the wicked, but only to form factions and seek promotion.

sentences.zh: 斯亦鄭朋、楊興之流，烏在其為剛直哉！

translations.literal: He too is of the sort of Zheng Peng and Yang Xing—wherein lies his being stern and upright!
translations.idiomatic: He belongs to the same breed as Zheng Peng and Yang Xing—where is the integrity in that!

sentences.zh: 人君者，察美惡，辨是非，賞以勸善，罰以懲奸，所以為治也。

translations.literal: The ruler of men examines beauty and ugliness, distinguishes right and wrong, rewards to encourage good, punishes to chastise wickedness—this is how he governs.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler examines good and evil, distinguishes right from wrong, rewards to encourage good conduct, and punishes to chastise wickedness—that is how he governs.

sentences.zh: 使豐言得實，則豐不當絀；

translations.literal: If Feng's words were substantiated, then Feng ought not have been demoted;
translations.idiomatic: If Feng's charges were true, then Feng ought not have been demoted;

sentences.zh: 若其誣罔，則堪、猛何辜焉！

translations.literal: if they were false and deceptive, then what crime had Kan and Meng!
translations.idiomatic: if they were false, then what crime had Kan and Meng committed!

sentences.zh: 今兩責而俱棄之，則美惡、是非果安在哉！

translations.literal: Now both are blamed and both are cast aside—then where in truth are beauty and ugliness, right and wrong!
translations.idiomatic: Now both parties are blamed and both are cast aside—then where do good and evil, right and wrong, actually lie!

sentences.zh: ----10賈捐之與楊興善。

translations.literal: ----10 Jia Juanzhi was on good terms with Yang Xing.
translations.idiomatic: ----10 Jia Juanzhi was on good terms with Yang Xing.

sentences.zh: 捐之數短石顯，以故不得官，稀復進見；

translations.literal: Juanzhi repeatedly spoke ill of Shi Xian and for this reason did not obtain office, rarely gaining audience again;
translations.idiomatic: Juanzhi repeatedly criticized Shi Xian and for that reason could not obtain office and rarely gained audience again;

sentences.zh: 興新以材能得幸。

translations.literal: Xing had newly been favored for talent and ability.
translations.idiomatic: Xing had newly been favored for his talent.

sentences.zh: 捐之謂興曰：「京兆尹缺，使我得見，言君蘭，京兆尹可立得。

translations.literal: Juanzhi said to Xing: "The Metropolitan Governorship is vacant; if you let me gain audience and speak for you, Lord Lan, the Metropolitan Governorship can be obtained at once.
translations.idiomatic: Juanzhi said to Xing, "The metropolitan governorship is vacant. If you let me gain audience and speak for you, Lord Lan, you can obtain the metropolitan governorship at once."

sentences.zh: 」興曰：「君房下筆，言語妙天下；

translations.literal: " Xing said: "Lord Fang, when you put pen to paper, your words are the wonder of All-under-Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: " Xing said, "Lord Fang, when you take up the brush your words are unmatched under Heaven;

sentences.zh: 使君房為尚書令，勝五鹿充宗遠甚。

translations.literal: if Lord Fang were made Director of the Masters of Writing, he would far surpass Wulu Chongzong.
translations.idiomatic: if you were made Director of the Masters of Writing, you would far surpass Wulu Chongzong.

sentences.zh: 」捐之曰：「令我得代充宗，君蘭為京兆，京兆，郡國首，尚書，百官本，天下真大治，士則不隔矣！

translations.literal: " Juanzhi said: "Let me replace Chongzong, and Lord Lan be Metropolitan Governor—Chang'an is the head of commanderies and kingdoms, the Masters of Writing are the root of the hundred officials; All-under-Heaven would truly be greatly governed, and scholars would not be blocked!
translations.idiomatic: " Juanzhi said, "Let me replace Chongzong and you, Lord Lan, become metropolitan governor. Chang'an is the head of the commanderies and kingdoms, and the Masters of Writing are the root of the hundred officials. Then the empire would truly be well governed and scholars would no longer be shut out!"

sentences.zh: 」捐之復短石顯，興曰：「顯方貴，上信用之；

translations.literal: " Juanzhi again spoke ill of Shi Xian; Xing said: "Xian is just now honored and the emperor trusts and employs him;
translations.idiomatic: " Juanzhi again criticized Shi Xian. Xing said, "Xian is at the height of power and the emperor trusts him;

sentences.zh: 今欲進，第從我計，且與合意，即得入矣！

translations.literal: if you now wish to advance, simply follow my plan—for the moment agree with his intent, and you can enter at once!
translations.idiomatic: if you wish to advance now, simply follow my plan—for the moment agree with him, and you can get in at once!"

sentences.zh: 」捐之即與興共為薦顯奏，稱譽其美，以為宜賜爵關內侯，引其兄弟以為諸曹；

translations.literal: " Juanzhi then together with Xing jointly drafted a memorial recommending Xian, praising his excellence, holding that he ought to be granted rank as Marquis within the Passes, and bringing in his brothers to serve in the various bureaus;
translations.idiomatic: " Juanzhi then joined Xing in drafting a memorial recommending Xian, praising his merits, proposing that he be granted rank as Marquis within the Passes, and bringing in his brothers to serve in the various bureaus;

sentences.zh: 又共為薦興奏，以為可試守京兆尹。

translations.literal: they also jointly drafted a memorial recommending Xing, holding that he could be tried as acting Metropolitan Governor.
translations.idiomatic: they also jointly drafted a memorial recommending Xing, proposing that he be tried as acting metropolitan governor.

sentences.zh: 石顯聞知，白之上，乃下興、捐之獄，令顯治之，奏「興，捐之懷詐偽，更相薦譽，欲得大位，罔上不道！

translations.literal: Shi Xian heard and knew, reported to the emperor, and thereupon sent Xing and Juanzhi down to prison, ordering Xian to prosecute them; he memorialized: "Xing and Juanzhi harbored deceit and falsity, mutually recommending and praising each other, wishing to obtain high position—deceiving the sovereign, undao!
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Xian learned of this, he reported it to the emperor. Xing and Juanzhi were sent to prison and Xian was ordered to prosecute them. He memorialized, "Xing and Juanzhi harbored deceit, praised each other in turn, and sought high office—deceiving the sovereign, a capital offense!"

sentences.zh: 」捐之竟坐棄市，興髡鉗為城旦。

translations.literal: " Juanzhi in the end was convicted and executed in the marketplace; Xing was shaved, fettered, and made a corvée laborer.
translations.idiomatic: " Juanzhi was in the end executed in the marketplace; Xing was shaved, fettered, and sentenced to corvée labor as a wall-builder.

sentences.zh: :臣光曰：君子以正攻邪，猶懼不克。

translations.literal: : Minister Guang said: The gentleman uses the upright to attack the wicked, yet still fears he may not overcome.
translations.idiomatic: : Minister Guang said: A gentleman uses rectitude to attack wickedness, yet still fears he may not prevail.

sentences.zh: 況捐之以邪攻邪，其能免乎！

translations.literal: How much more when Juanzhi used wickedness to attack wickedness—how could he escape!
translations.idiomatic: How much less can one who uses wickedness to attack wickedness, as Juanzhi did, hope to escape!

sentences.zh: ----11徙清河王竟為中山王。

translations.literal: ----11 King Jing of Qinghe was moved to become King of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: ----11 King Jing of Qinghe was moved to become King of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: ----12匈奴呼韓邪單于民眾益盛，塞下禽獸盡，單于足以自衛，不畏郅支，其大臣多勸單于北歸者。

translations.literal: ----12 Among the Xiongnu, Chanyu Huhanye's masses grew ever more prosperous; beasts below the frontier passes were exhausted; the chanyu was sufficient to defend himself and did not fear Zhizhi; many of his great ministers urged the chanyu to return north.
translations.idiomatic: ----12 Among the Xiongnu, Chanyu Huhanye's following grew ever stronger; game below the frontier passes was exhausted; the chanyu had enough strength to defend himself and no longer feared Zhizhi; and many of his great ministers urged him to return north.

sentences.zh: 久之，單于竟北歸庭，民眾稍稍歸之，其國遂定。

translations.literal: After a long time, the chanyu at last returned north to his court; the masses gradually returned to him, and his state was thereby settled.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time the chanyu at last returned north to his court; his people gradually came back to him, and his state was thereby settled.

sentences.zh: 1春，二月，赦天下。

translations.literal: 1 Spring, second month, amnesty for All-under-Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In spring, the second month, an amnesty was proclaimed for the empire.

sentences.zh: ----2丁酉，御史大夫韋玄成為丞相；

translations.literal: ----2 On dingyou, Censor-in-Chief Wei Xuancheng became chancellor;
translations.idiomatic: ----2 On dingyou, Censor-in-Chief Wei Xuancheng became chancellor;

sentences.zh: 右扶風鄭弘為御史大夫。

translations.literal: Zheng Hong of Right Fufeng became censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Hong of Right Fufeng became censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: ----3三月，壬戌朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: ----3 Third month, on the first day renxu, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 In the third month, on the first day renxu, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: ----4夏，六月，赦天下。

translations.literal: ----4 Summer, sixth month, amnesty for All-under-Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 In summer, the sixth month, an amnesty was proclaimed for the empire.

sentences.zh: ----5上問給事中匡衡以地震日食之變，衡上疏曰：「陛下躬聖德，開太平之路，閔愚吏民觸法抵禁，比年大赦，使百姓得改行自新，天下幸甚！

translations.literal: ----5 The emperor questioned Palace Attendant Kuang Heng on the changes of earthquake and solar eclipse; Heng submitted a memorial saying: "Your Majesty personally embodies sage virtue, opens the road of great peace, pities foolish officials and people who touch the law and reach prohibition; in successive years great amnesties have let the common people reform conduct and renew themselves—All-under-Heaven is greatly fortunate!
translations.idiomatic: ----5 The emperor questioned Palace Attendant Kuang Heng about the earthquake and solar eclipse. Heng submitted a memorial saying, "Your Majesty personally embodies sage virtue and opens the road to great peace. You pity foolish officials and common people who stumble into the law. Year after year you have proclaimed great amnesties so the people may reform and renew themselves—the empire is greatly fortunate!"

sentences.zh: 臣竊見大赦之後，奸邪不為衰止，今日大赦，明日犯法，相隨入獄，此殆導之未得其務也。

translations.literal: Your subject has privately seen that after great amnesties the wicked do not decline and stop; today a great amnesty, tomorrow violating the law—they follow one another into prison; this is probably that guidance has not obtained its proper task.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has observed that after great amnesties wicked conduct does not decline. Today there is a great amnesty, tomorrow people break the law again and enter prison in succession—this probably means guidance has not hit its mark.

sentences.zh: 今天下俗，貪財賤義，好聲色，上侈靡，親戚之恩薄，婚姻之黨隆，苟合徼幸，以身設利；

translations.literal: Now the customs of All-under-Heaven: they value wealth and slight righteousness, delight in sound and color, exalt extravagance and excess, kinship grace is thin, marriage factions are exalted, they hastily join and seek fortune, setting up profit with their persons;
translations.idiomatic: The customs of the empire today value wealth and slight righteousness, delight in pleasure and display, exalt extravagance, thin kinship ties, exalt marriage factions, join hastily and seek lucky breaks, and set up profit for themselves;

sentences.zh: 不改其原，雖歲赦之，刑猶難使錯而不用也，臣愚以為宜壹曠然大變其俗。

translations.literal: if their root is not changed, though amnestied every year, punishments still can hardly make errors unused; your subject foolishly thinks one ought with unified breadth greatly to transform their customs.
translations.idiomatic: and unless the root is changed, even yearly amnesties will not make punishments fall idle. Your subject foolishly thinks the customs ought to be transformed all at once and on a grand scale.

sentences.zh: 夫朝廷者，天下之楨幹也。

translations.literal: Now the court is the main pillar of All-under-Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The court is the main pillar of the empire.

sentences.zh: 朝有變色之言，則下有爭鬥之患；

translations.literal: If at court there are words that change countenance, then below there is the trouble of contention and fighting;
translations.idiomatic: If at court there are words that change men's faces, below there will be strife;

sentences.zh: 上有自專之士，則下有不讓之人；

translations.literal: if above there are self-willed scholars, then below there are men who do not yield;
translations.idiomatic: if above there are self-willed men, below there will be men who refuse to yield;

sentences.zh: 上有克勝之佐，則下有傷害之心；

translations.literal: if above there are assistants who overcome and triumph, then below there are hearts that injure and harm;
translations.idiomatic: if above there are assistants who love to overcome others, below there will be hearts bent on injury;

sentences.zh: 上有好利之臣，則下有盜竊之民；

translations.literal: if above there are ministers who love profit, then below there are people who steal and rob;
translations.idiomatic: if above there are ministers who love profit, below there will be thieves among the people;

sentences.zh: 此其本也。

translations.literal: this is its root.
translations.idiomatic: that is the root of it.

sentences.zh: 治天下者，審所上而已。

translations.literal: He who governs All-under-Heaven need only examine whom he elevates.
translations.idiomatic: He who governs the empire need only examine whom he elevates.

sentences.zh: 教化之流，非家至而人說之也；

translations.literal: The flow of transforming instruction is not reaching every house and having people speak it;
translations.idiomatic: The flow of transforming instruction does not come from visiting every house and preaching to each person;

sentences.zh: 賢者在位，能者布職，朝廷崇禮，百僚敬讓，道德之行，由內及外，自近者始，然後民知所法，遷善日進而不自知也。

translations.literal: the worthy are in position, the able spread their duties, the court honors ritual, the hundred officials are respectful and yielding, the practice of virtue proceeds from within to without, beginning with what is near—only then do the people know what to take as law, move toward good daily advancing without themselves knowing it.
translations.idiomatic: the worthy hold office, the able perform their duties, the court honors ritual, the hundred officials are respectful and yielding, and the practice of virtue spreads from within outward, beginning with what is near—only then do the people know what to follow, advance toward good daily, and do so without even knowing it.

sentences.zh: 《詩》曰：『商邑翼翼，四方之極。

translations.literal: The Odes says: 'The Shang capital is solemn and strong, the utmost of the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes says, "The Shang capital stands solemn and strong, the model for the four quarters."

sentences.zh: 』今長安，天子之都，親承聖化，然其習俗無以異於遠方，郡國來者無所法則，或見侈靡而放效之；

translations.literal: ' Now Chang'an, the Son of Heaven's capital, personally receives sage transformation—yet its customs are no different from distant regions; those who come from commanderies and kingdoms have no model to follow, or they see extravagance and imitate it;
translations.idiomatic: " Yet Chang'an, the Son of Heaven's capital, personally receives sage transformation, yet its customs are no different from distant regions. Visitors from the commanderies and kingdoms find no model to follow, or they see extravagance and imitate it;

sentences.zh: 此教化之原本，風俗之樞機，宜先正者也。

translations.literal: this is the root origin of transforming instruction, the pivot of customs—what ought first be rectified.
translations.idiomatic: this is the root of transforming instruction and the pivot of custom—what ought to be rectified first.

sentences.zh: 臣聞天人之際，精祲有以相蕩，善惡有以相推，事作乎下者象動乎上，陰變則靜者動，陽蔽則明者晻，水旱之災隨類而至。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that between Heaven and man, essences and vapors have means to stir each other; good and evil have means to push each other; affairs arising below are mirrored in movement above—when yin changes, what was still moves; when yang is blocked, what was bright grows dim; flood and drought disasters arrive according to their kinds.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has heard that between Heaven and man essences and vapors stir one another, good and evil push one another, and affairs arising below are mirrored in movement above—when yin shifts, what was still moves; when yang is blocked, what was bright grows dim; flood and drought follow in their kinds.

sentences.zh: 陛下祗畏天戒，哀閔元元，宜省靡麗，考制度，近忠正，遠巧佞，以崇至仁，匡失俗，道德弘於京師，淑問揚乎疆外，然後大化可成，禮讓可興也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty reverently fears Heaven's warnings, pities and commiserates with the black-haired people—you ought to reduce extravagance and splendor, examine institutions, draw near the loyal and upright, send far the crafty and sycophantic, thereby to exalt utmost benevolence and correct failing customs; when virtue and the Way are magnified in the capital and good report spreads beyond the borders, then great transformation can be achieved and courtesy and yielding can be raised.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty reverently heeds Heaven's warnings and pities the common people. You ought to reduce extravagance, examine institutions, draw near the loyal and upright, send away the crafty and sycophantic, exalt utmost benevolence, and correct failing customs. When virtue is magnified in the capital and good report spreads beyond the borders, then great transformation can be achieved and courtesy and yielding can flourish.

sentences.zh: 」上說其言，遷衡為光祿大夫。

translations.literal: " The emperor was pleased with his words and transferred Heng to be Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was pleased with his words and transferred Heng to Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: :荀悅論曰：夫赦者，權時之宜，非常典也。

translations.literal: : Xun Yue's discussion says: Now amnesty is a timely expedient, not a constant statute.
translations.idiomatic: : Xun Yue's discussion says: Amnesty is a timely expedient, not a standing institution.

sentences.zh: 漢興，承秦兵革之後，大愚之世，比屋可刑，故設三章之法，大赦之令，蕩滌穢流，與民更始，時勢然也。

translations.literal: When Han arose, inheriting after Qin's arms and armor, in an age of great ignorance where house by house could be punished, therefore the law of three chapters was established and the order of great amnesty—washing away foul currents and making a fresh start with the people; the times were so.
translations.idiomatic: When Han arose, inheriting the aftermath of Qin's wars, in an age of great ignorance where almost every household could be punished, the law of three chapters and orders of great amnesty were established to wash away foul currents and make a fresh start with the people—the times required it.

sentences.zh: 後世承業，襲而不革，失時宜矣。

translations.literal: Later generations inherited the enterprise and followed without reform—losing the timely fit.
translations.idiomatic: Later generations inherited the practice and followed it without reform—missing the timely fit.

sentences.zh: 若惠、文之世，無所赦之。

translations.literal: In ages such as those of Emperor Hui and Emperor Wen, there was nothing to amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In ages such as those of Emperors Hui and Wen, there was nothing to amnesty.

sentences.zh: 若孝景之時，七國皆亂，異心並起，奸詐非一；

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xiaojing, the seven states all rebelled, divergent hearts arose together, treachery and deceit were not one alone;
translations.idiomatic: In the time of Emperor Xiaojing the seven states all rebelled, divergent hearts arose together, and treachery was manifold;

sentences.zh: 及武帝末年，賦役繁興，群盜並起，加以太子之事，巫蠱之禍，天下紛然，百姓無聊，人不自安；

translations.literal: and by the late years of Emperor Wu, levies and corvée flourished, bandit gangs arose together, added to the affair of the heir apparent and the disaster of witchcraft—All-under-Heaven was in turmoil, the common people had no relief, men could not find security in themselves;
translations.idiomatic: and by the late years of Emperor Wu levies and corvée multiplied, bandit gangs arose together, and there were added the affair of the heir apparent and the disaster of witchcraft—All-under-Heaven was in turmoil, the people had no relief, and no one felt secure;

sentences.zh: 及光武之際，撥亂之後：如此之比，宜為赦矣。

translations.literal: and at the time of Emperor Guangwu, after settling disorder—cases like these ought to have amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: and at the time of Emperor Guangwu, after settling disorder—times like these called for amnesty.

sentences.zh: ----6秋，七月，隴西羌彡姐旁種反，詔召丞相韋玄成等入議。

translations.literal: ----6 Autumn, seventh month, the Qiang of the Shan-jie collateral lineage in Longxi rebelled; an edict summoned Chancellor Wei Xuancheng and others to enter for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: ----6 In autumn, the seventh month, the Qiang of the Shan-jie collateral lineage in Longxi rebelled; an edict summoned Chancellor Wei Xuancheng and others to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 是時，歲比不登，朝廷方以為憂，而遭羌變，玄成等漠然，莫有對者。

translations.literal: At this time, year after year harvests did not succeed; the court was just taking it as worry, yet encountered the Qiang disturbance—Xuancheng and the others were blank, none having a reply.
translations.idiomatic: At this time harvests had failed year after year and the court was already worried when the Qiang disturbance struck. Xuancheng and the others sat blankly, with no one able to reply.

sentences.zh: 右將軍馮奉世曰：「羌虜近在竟內背畔，不以時誅，無以威制遠蠻，臣願帥師討之！

translations.literal: General of the Right Feng Fengshi said: "The Qiang barbarians are near, rebelling within the frontier—if not executed in season, there is no means to awe and control distant barbarians; your subject wishes to lead troops to punish them!
translations.idiomatic: General of the Right Feng Fengshi said, "The Qiang are near at hand, rebelling within the frontier. If they are not punished promptly, there is no way to awe distant barbarians. Your subject wishes to lead troops to punish them!"

sentences.zh: 」上問用兵之數，對曰：「臣聞善用兵者，役不再興，糧不三載，故師不久暴而天誅亟決。

translations.literal: " The emperor asked the numbers for employing troops; he replied: "Your subject has heard that one who skillfully uses troops does not raise corvée twice or transport grain three times; therefore armies do not long rage abroad while Heaven's punishment is swiftly decided.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor asked how many troops would be needed. He replied, "Your subject has heard that one who skillfully uses troops does not raise corvée twice or transport grain three times. Therefore armies should not long rage abroad while Heaven's punishment is swiftly decided."

sentences.zh: 往者數不料敵，而師至於折傷，再三發調，則曠日煩費，威武虧矣。

translations.literal: In the past, several times the enemy was not measured and armies came to broken injury; repeatedly issuing levies then wastes days and troubles expense, and martial prestige is diminished.
translations.idiomatic: In the past we several times misjudged the enemy and armies were broken. Repeated levies waste time and money and diminish martial prestige.

sentences.zh: 今反虜無慮三萬人，法當倍，用六萬人。

translations.literal: Now the rebel barbarians are estimated at no less than thirty thousand men; by rule one ought to double and employ sixty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Now the rebels are estimated at no less than thirty thousand men. By rule one ought to double that and employ sixty thousand.

sentences.zh: 然羌戎，弓矛之兵耳，器不犀利，可用四萬人。

translations.literal: Yet the Qiang and Rong are only bow-and-spear troops; their weapons are not sharp and keen—forty thousand can be employed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Qiang and Rong are only bow-and-spear fighters; their weapons are not sharp—forty thousand should suffice.

sentences.zh: 一月足以決。

translations.literal: One month is sufficient to decide it.
translations.idiomatic: One month should be enough to settle it.

sentences.zh: 」丞相、御史、兩將軍皆以為：「民方收斂時未可多發，發萬人屯守之，且足。

translations.literal: " The chancellor, censor, and both generals all held: "The people are just at harvest time and cannot be levied in great numbers; send ten thousand to garrison and defend—that will suffice for now.
translations.idiomatic: " The chancellor, censor, and both generals all held, "The people are just at harvest time and cannot be levied in great numbers. Send ten thousand to garrison the frontier—that will suffice for now."

sentences.zh: 」奉世曰：「不可。

translations.literal: " Fengshi said: "It cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: " Fengshi said, "That will not do."

sentences.zh: 天下被饑饉，士馬羸耗，守戰之備久廢不簡，夷狄有輕邊吏之心，而羌首難。

translations.literal: All-under-Heaven suffers famine; soldiers and horses are emaciated and spent; preparations for defense and battle have long been abandoned and not examined; the Yi and Di have hearts that slight frontier officials—and the Qiang are foremost in difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: The empire suffers famine; soldiers and horses are worn down; defenses have long been neglected; the barbarians already look down on frontier officials—and the Qiang are the hardest of them.

sentences.zh: 今以萬人分屯數處，虜見兵少，必不畏懼。

translations.literal: Now with ten thousand divided and garrisoned in several places, when the barbarians see few troops they will surely not fear.
translations.idiomatic: If ten thousand are divided and garrisoned in several places, the enemy will see how few the troops are and surely will not fear them.

sentences.zh: 戰則挫兵病師，守則百姓不救，如此，怯弱之形見。

translations.literal: If they fight, troops are broken and armies fall ill; if they defend, the common people are not rescued—thus the form of timidity and weakness appears.
translations.idiomatic: If they fight, the army will be broken; if they only defend, the people cannot be rescued. In that way weakness will be plain for all to see.

sentences.zh: 羌人乘利，諸種並和，相扇而起，臣恐中國之役不得止於四萬，非財幣所能解也。

translations.literal: The Qiang will seize the advantage; the various tribes will join in harmony, fanning one another to rise; your subject fears the empire's campaign will not stop at forty thousand, and it cannot be resolved by wealth and currency alone.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang will seize the advantage, the various tribes will join together and fan one another into revolt. Your subject fears the empire's campaign will not stop at forty thousand men, and money alone cannot solve it.

sentences.zh: 故少發師而曠日，與一舉而疾決，利害相萬也。

translations.literal: Therefore to send few troops and waste days, versus one effort and swift decision—the benefit and harm differ ten thousandfold.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore to send few troops and waste days, versus one effort and swift decision—the difference in benefit and harm is ten thousandfold.

sentences.zh: 」固爭之，不能得。

translations.literal: " He firmly contended but could not obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: " He argued firmly but could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 有詔，益二千人。

translations.literal: An edict was issued increasing by two thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued to add two thousand men.

sentences.zh: 於是遣奉世將萬二千人騎，以將屯為名，典屬國任立、護軍都尉韓昌為偏裨，到隴西，分屯三處。

translations.literal: Thereupon Fengshi was sent leading twelve thousand cavalry, under the name of a garrison commandant, with Director of Dependent States Ren Li and Protector Army Commandant Han Chang as flank assistants; they reached Longxi and divided garrisons in three places.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Fengshi was sent leading twelve thousand cavalry under the title of garrison commandant, with Director of Dependent States Ren Li and Protector Army Commandant Han Chang as flank assistants. They reached Longxi and divided garrisons in three places.

sentences.zh: 昌先遣兩校尉與羌戰，羌虜盛多，皆為所破，殺兩校尉。

translations.literal: Han Chang first sent two commandants to fight the Qiang; the Qiang barbarians were numerous and strong, and both were broken by them—the two commandants were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Han Chang first sent two commandants to fight the Qiang. The enemy were numerous and strong, both units were defeated, and the two commandants were killed.

sentences.zh: 奉世具上地形部眾多少之計，願益三萬六千人，乃足以決事。

translations.literal: Fengshi fully reported up a plan of terrain and numbers of divisions and masses, wishing to add thirty-six thousand men—only then would it suffice to decide the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Fengshi reported in full on the terrain and troop strength and asked for thirty-six thousand more men, saying only then would the affair be settled.

sentences.zh: 書奏，天子大為發兵六萬餘人。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the Son of Heaven greatly raised troops of more than sixty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the emperor greatly raised an army of more than sixty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 八月，拜太常弋陽侯任千秋為奮武將軍以助之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Ren Qianqiu, Marquis of Yiyang and Grand Master of Ceremonies, was appointed General Who Displays Martial Might to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Ren Qianqiu, Marquis of Yiyang and Grand Master of Ceremonies, was appointed General Who Displays Martial Might to assist him.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，兵畢至隴西，十一月，並進，羌虜大破，斬首數千級，餘皆走出塞。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, the troops all arrived at Longxi; in the eleventh month they advanced together. The Qiang barbarians were greatly defeated; heads cut numbered several thousand; the remainder all fled out beyond the frontier passes.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, the troops all reached Longxi; in the eleventh month they advanced together. The Qiang were routed, several thousand heads were taken, and the rest all fled beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 兵未決間，漢復發募士萬人，拜定襄太守韓安國為建威將軍，未進，聞羌破而還。

translations.literal: While the campaign was not yet decided, Han again raised and recruited ten thousand men, appointing Han Anguo, Administrator of Dingxiang, as General Who Establishes Might. He had not advanced when he heard the Qiang were broken and returned.
translations.idiomatic: While the campaign was still undecided, Han again recruited ten thousand men and appointed Han Anguo, Administrator of Dingxiang, as General Who Establishes Might. He had not advanced when he heard the Qiang were defeated and returned.

sentences.zh: 詔罷吏士，頗留屯田，備要害處。

translations.literal: An edict dismissed officers and soldiers, but many were left for garrison-farming to guard strategic points.
translations.idiomatic: An edict dismissed the officers and soldiers, but many were left to garrison-farm and guard strategic points.

translations.literal: category: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
translations.idiomatic: category: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
